40e07960-2c59-5c21-8ff8-0aa9645bf0eb.name: Postcards showing Romanian tourists in Egypt
40e07960-2c59-5c21-8ff8-0aa9645bf0eb.short_description: In the 19th century, North Africa was mostly known to Romanians from geography schoolbooks and newspaper articles. However, starting from the middle of the 19th century there are information about wealthy Romanians who visited North African countries, some of them recounting in their memoirs their African experiences. For example, Romanian poet and politician Vasile Alecsandri visited in September-October 1853 the Moroccan ports of Tangier and Tétouan and published his impressions in a Romanian literary periodical. A bit more than half a century later, four Romanian students entered an international competition for travelling by foot 100,000 km. In July 1911 they reached Egypt, where they visited Cairo, the pyramids, the Valley of the Kings, Memphis, Luxor, Karnak, Aswan, the Abu Simbel temples.

416183bd-8afc-5737-8b32-4fcbb3e2e553.name: Ali ben Ghedhahem's seal
416183bd-8afc-5737-8b32-4fcbb3e2e553.short_description: This seal, dating to 1864, belonged to 'Ali ben Ghedhahem, an educated man and the son of a qadi from the Kasserine region. He was one of the biggest figures in an insurrection triggered by the issuing of a decree to double taxes in Mejba, April 1864. The revolt started in the west, but quickly spread to the whole regency, with the exception of just a few coastal towns. However, it was soon qashed, and the violent suppression the people were subjected was not forgotten until the mid-20th century. The legendary hero 'Ali ben Ghedhahem was arrested and convicted.
416183bd-8afc-5737-8b32-4fcbb3e2e553.holder: Institut Supérieur d’Histoire Contemporaine de la Tunisie

41a2680e-8cf9-5ee5-a679-4297b5a1558c.name: Fındıklı
41a2680e-8cf9-5ee5-a679-4297b5a1558c.short_description: Pascal Sébah (1823-1886) was a pioneer photographer who worked in Istanbul. In 1857 he opened his first photography studio, *El Chark Societe Photographic*, in Istanbul and by 1873 was successful enough to open another studio in Cairo. In 1860 he moved to another studio next to the Russian Embassy in order to work with A. Laroche, who worked in Paris. He continued to work with Laroche until 1873.

41c0d246-c999-5ff4-8002-64210176e2eb.name: An old exhibition from Tiled Kiosk
41c0d246-c999-5ff4-8002-64210176e2eb.short_description: The Tiled Kiosk is a pavilion set within the outer walls of Topkapı Palace that dates from 1472. It was built by the Ottoman sultan Mehmed II as a pleasure palace or kiosk. The building was used as the Imperial Museum between 1875 and 1891. In 1953, it was opened to the public as a museum of Turkish and Islamic art, and was later incorporated into the Istanbul Archaeology Museums. The collections of the Tiled Kiosk Museum consist of about 2000 artefacts belonging to the Seljuk and Ottoman eras, dating from the 11th-20th centuries. These artefacts include those that existed when the museum was incorporated into the İstanbul Archaeological Museums due to its proximity as well as those acquired through excavations, purchases, donations and confiscations.
41c0d246-c999-5ff4-8002-64210176e2eb.dates: The Tiled Kiosk: 15th century; The photograph: 19th century
keywords: Istanbul Archaeological Museum; Tiled Kiosk

427783d7-27c6-57e4-9e7c-ee894a6d6e9d.name: The Hotel Excelsior at the Lido in Venice at the end of construction work
427783d7-27c6-57e4-9e7c-ee894a6d6e9d.short_description: The photograph shows the Hotel Excelsior on the beach of the Lido sandbar which separates the Venice lagoon from the sea. The building appears to be almost finished but not yet open: since the hotel was inaugurated in 1908, the photograph was probably shot before then. Giovanni Sardi was one of the most gifted architects of the eclectic generation. Here, he uses elements of the Moorish architecture like minarets and domes mixed with decorations in the Art Nouveau style and medieval elements, to emphasize the character of the building as a fabulous place for holidays and amusement.

42a328aa-1821-5971-b533-2606dafaee02.name: The excavation of Mount Nemrut
42a328aa-1821-5971-b533-2606dafaee02.short_description: In the 19th century, efforts were in place to modernize the Ottoman Empire, as many of the leading statesmen were exposed to Western ideas through education and travel. The museum was founded by decree in 1891 as the Imperial Museum. The first curator and founder of the museum was Osman Hamdi. Hamdi began construction of the main building in 1881, and it achieved its present neo-Greek form in 1908. The architect was Alexander Vallaury. It is one of the prominent structures built in the neoclassical style in Istanbul. Osman Hamdi, during his tenure as museum director, launched the first Turkish scientific excavations. He carried out archaeological excavations at Mount Nemrut, Laguna and Sidon.
keywords: Painting; Osman Hamdi Bey; orientalist Turkish painters; archaeological excavations

430c3094-96d5-556b-b26c-13d08bce78c4.name: Vue générale de la station de Beyrouth, published between 1900 and 1905. (General view of the Beirut Station)
430c3094-96d5-556b-b26c-13d08bce78c4.description: Beirut Railway Station, today known as Mar Mikhael Station, was established in 1895 on the eastern outskirts of Beirut for the Beirut–Damascus railway. The two-storey station, with its tiled hipped roof, was based on a French railway architectural model associated with the Paris–Lyon–Méditerranée network, then adapted to Beirut's climate and local requirements. It was built in a farmland area between the Mar Mikhael (Saint Michael) church, an area that would be developed later and become part of Beirut's urban landscape. The station was damaged in the 2020 port explosion in Beirut. A restoration and rehabilitation project was announced in 2023 by UNESCO and Italy as part of the LiBeirut initiative.

4318dbfb-9a52-562e-8cea-6daf8a6a9d78.name: Rumelia Railway
4318dbfb-9a52-562e-8cea-6daf8a6a9d78.short_description: During the 19th century, new technologies radically transformed both travel and communications. The first railway in Anatolia was constructed between Izmir and Aydin. Ottoman railways were mainly built during the period of Abdülhamid II. The first railway in the Republic of Turkey was part of the İzmir-Aydın line, founded by a British company in 1860. The İzmir-Kasaba line was built in 1865, the Rumeli line in 1869-77, the Anatolia-Baghdad line in 1872 and the Mudanya-Bursa line in 1892.

43b2594e-92cf-584f-b624-afc4b94a968d.short_description: Portrait of Giovanni Miani (1810–1872). Born in Northern Italy, he was an intellectual who was forced by Austrian authorities to seek exile in the Ottoman Empire. He lived in Athens, Smyrna and Egypt and was one of the European explorers who tried to find the sources of the Nile.

450cc7be-20ef-52cc-862c-1aa33641995b.name: Muslim soldiers of the Austro-Hungarian infantry-regiment N°3 from Bosnia-Herzegovina in a special room for worshipping
450cc7be-20ef-52cc-862c-1aa33641995b.short_description: This picture shows Bosnian soldiers praying in a room in a barracks in Budapest. The third Bosnian infantry regiment recruited in Tuzla was stationed there. In 1882, the Austro-Hungarian administration of Bosnia-Herzegovina created four Bosnian infantry regiments. Because 50 per cent of the Bosnian population was Muslim, the Austro-Hungarian Army supported the free exercise of the religion amongst its soldiers.

453156d3-f141-581a-96a5-4ef8c83cbae1.name: Dr Charles Nicolle
453156d3-f141-581a-96a5-4ef8c83cbae1.short_description: Pictured here is Dr. Charles Nicolle, a French microbiology doctor born in Rouen on 21 September 1966, in his research laboratory. His name is strongly linked to l'Institut Pasteur, which he directed from 1903–1936, playing the role of administrator, researcher, school headmaster, and advocate for the teaching of hygiene and illness prevention. In 1928 he received the Nobel Prize for Physiology. He died in 1936 and is buried at the Institut Pasteur, where his tombstone is engraved with olive and apple tree branches crossed over, the symbols of Tunisia and Normandy.

4541475a-b5b3-51f1-9463-7a0141b6de58.name: Mohamed Daghabi
4541475a-b5b3-51f1-9463-7a0141b6de58.short_description: Born in El Hamma to the Beni Zid tribe (near Gabès), Mohamed Daghbagi (1885–1924) became a deserter in 1915, after the battle of Dhibat between the French troops and the Tunisian resistance. In 1920 he rose to fame through his role in an armed group which took part in various conflicts. He then took refuge in Tripolitaine, and was arrested in 1922 and given back to the French. He was executed in El Hamma on 1 March 1924.

45f8402d-e18b-5199-b2ae-ecde35d016ae.name: The train for VIP guests used during the inauguration of Luxor–Aswan Railway Line
45f8402d-e18b-5199-b2ae-ecde35d016ae.short_description:
The inauguration of the Aswan Train Station, with \`Adli Yakan Pasha; Muhammad Najib al-Gharabli Pasha; Husayn Rushdi Pasha; Tharwat Pasha; Fathallah Barakat Pasha; Morkos Hanna Pasha; al-Dagwi Bek, director of Aswan; and Mahmud Shakir Bek, deputy undersecretary of the Ministry of Transportation in attendance. 460ecb9a-1f86-59fa-b384-df26f5b5b4fa.name: The Chinese quarter at Cormeilles-en-Parisis
460ecb9a-1f86-59fa-b384-df26f5b5b4fa.short_description: The first wave of Chinese immigration to France was in 1916, when the Chinese government signed a treaty to send 35,000 Chinese citizens to work in France. This first small group, who had settled mainly in the regions around Paris, was followed by a second wave in the 1930s. Badly paid, and living in makeshift accommodation, these Chinese immigrants were mostly given heavy manual work.

462d8120-9ece-5f2c-b1f7-e362d936bd2d.name: L'École de la Rue du Pacha (classrooom exit)
462d8120-9ece-5f2c-b1f7-e362d936bd2d.short_description: The school founded by Louise-Renée-Millet, opened 1 May 1900, was the first public school for young Muslim girls. Pictured here are the young girls as they enter school, veiled, accompanied and under the strict gaze of their French teachers. Subsidised by the French Resident-General until it was taken over by a *habous*, the school came under the government's jurisdiction between 1911 and 1912, and was then moved to a new residence on the Rue du Pacha. Despite its humble beginnings, with just five students, the school steadily expanded. Nabeul, Sousse, and Kairouan, on the inside of the country, soon followed suit and opened their own public schools. L'École de la Rue du Pacha held the held the important position as the first school of its kind, as well as the cradle for many important members of the first generation of political militants and feminist activists.

4637b883-3f04-595d-8275-01f5645225cb.name: La gare Midan, Damas (The Midan Station, Damascus)
4637b883-3f04-595d-8275-01f5645225cb.description: The Midan Station is located south of Damascus in Al Midan neighbourhood. It predates both the Qadam and Qanawat stations and was the first railway station to be built in Damascus. The Midan Station was part of the region's earliest railway network owned by the French company Société des Chemins de fer Ottomans Économiques de Beyrouth-Damas-Hauran en Syrie, later known as Damas-Hama et Prolongements (D.H.P.). The company's first railway, the Hauran Railway (Damascus–Muzairib), opened in 1894. During the planning of the Hijaz Railway, unsuccessful attempts were made to purchase the Hauran Railway. As a result, a parallel railway line was constructed, and both lines remained in operation until the First World War, when foreign-owned railways belonging to companies based in enemy territory were confiscated. This included the Hauran Railway, whose operation was subsequently transferred to the Hijaz Railway.

464aad1f-7be1-5c39-ab67-b2b1cb16454a.name: General meeting on women's suffrage
464aad1f-7be1-5c39-ab67-b2b1cb16454a.short_description: Throughout the 19th and early 20th centuries, a number of different political movements for votes for women emerged, all using many different tactics. For example in May 1908, following the English model, a group of "suffragettes" held a protest during the Paris municipal elections, in which their actions (upturning ballot boxes, breaking polling station windows) were controversial. The following month, a national congress on women's rights and suffrage was held in Paris, an act which was hugely symbolic in and of itself. Their struggle was a long one, and it was not until 1944 that French women obtained the right to vote, which they exercised for the first time in 1945.
keywords: Women; right to vote; France

47088250-c322-5a2f-8bb2-03e71b5faa1d.name: Materials found in the Kamiros excavations in Rodi
47088250-c322-5a2f-8bb2-03e71b5faa1d.short_description: Total view of materials chosen by Luigi Pernier, director of Archaeological School of Athens, from the excavation in Kamiros area (Rhodes) in 1912. Pernier decided to send part of the findings to the Prehistoric and Ethnographic Museum in Rome founded by Luigi Pigorini. These materials include mainly grave goods.

47ae1491-a4bf-5c5f-98f7-d10504afcb6c.description: Photographic print that is part of an album of different Istanbul images taken by the studio of the three Armenian brothers who, in 1880, opened a headquarters in this city. 47f1e835-2989-56cc-b52c-52619991c2a5.name: Italian military conscription office in Tunis
47f1e835-2989-56cc-b52c-52619991c2a5.short_description: Under terms of an 1896 agreement with France, Italy ran a military conscription office in Tunis. It was through this office that Italy drafted its migrants in Tunisia for the war on Turkey in 1911-12 and for the First World War. During WWI, many Italians living in Tunisia, because of their knowledge of the French language.  were assigned to the military units posted in France. Many of them died or were crippled for life. After the war, the Italian government opened a War Pensions Bureau in Tunis.
47f1e835-2989-56cc-b52c-52619991c2a5.author: Massimo Sanacore

4859f5a8-7af7-59f7-8271-982ef083627b.name: *Fellahs* (peasants) use a *shadouf* to draw water from the Nile from a well.
4859f5a8-7af7-59f7-8271-982ef083627b.short_description: Ernest Benecke (1817–1894), a French photographer of Anglo-German origins, was one of the first to be interested in the people rather than the monuments he saw during his travels in the Middle East. His pictures foreground daily life, as we can see from this photograph, which was taken in Egypt and shows a traditional mode of irrigation using the *shadouf*, a weighted appliance which allowed water to be poured from a well over a field.

48a64aba-b279-5473-911b-51ced2c8a938.name: Portrait Album – Ottoman State Officers
48a64aba-b279-5473-911b-51ced2c8a938.short_description: With the political developments of the 19th century, interest in the East increased steadily in the western world. Everything belonging to the East was the centre of interest for western observers. As a result, close to 160 artists visited Istanbul in the 19th century. Pascal Sébah (1823-86) was a pioneer photographer who worked in Istanbul. Sébah opened a photography studio known as "El Chark " in Pera in 1857. The studio's most successful period started with the Vienna Universal Exhibition in 1873. Sébah formed a partnership with Joaillier Polycarpe in 1885. In 1899, the two partners bought Abdullah Frères's archives. For the Vienna Universal Exhibition in 1873, Pascal Sébah prepared *The Ottoman Clothing Album* to be exhibited at the Ottoman Stand.
48a64aba-b279-5473-911b-51ced2c8a938.holder: Istanbul University, Nadir Eserler Kütüphanesi (Rare Books Library)

48f017b2-30fc-5195-8291-3ffaa1a2aeb8.name: Repairing pyramids road, Cairo
48f017b2-30fc-5195-8291-3ffaa1a2aeb8.short_description: The Pyramids Road was fully repaired and put into use in 1868, successfully joining Giza to Cairo. Thanks to rising tourism in the area, different modes of transport were introduced along this route: cabs and omnibuses in the 19th century, and a tramway in the 20th century. The road was finally resurfaced following the invention of the motorcar, as we can see in this photograph.

49a80737-c924-5479-8273-7392e3cd1db8.name: Gjorgij Pulevski
49a80737-c924-5479-8273-7392e3cd1db8.short_description: Gjorgji Pulevski was a prominent figure of the Macedonian Enlightenment. He was born in Galichnik in 1822 and died in Sofia in 1893. In 1873, during his stay in Belgrade, he published the ”Dictionary of Four Languages,” which included Macedonian, Albanian, Greek and Turkish words. His “Dictionary of Three Languages” was issued in 1875. Gjorgji Pulevski was the founder of the Macedonian Literary Society, established in Sofia in 1888. It was one of the independent associations of Macedonian emigrants that made contributions to the awakening of the Macedonian national spirit.
49a80737-c924-5479-8273-7392e3cd1db8.author: Nada Andonovska (author), Dragan Georgiev, historian (consultant)
keywords: Enlightenment

49ebcfec-7199-5c0b-94f3-8ed498d743df.name: Archaeological excavations

49fa2453-a0f1-50d3-9c2e-b116b3fe9fdd.name: Frith photograph
49fa2453-a0f1-50d3-9c2e-b116b3fe9fdd.short_description: Francis Frith was one of the most successful commercial photographers from the 1850s and 1860s. He also established what was to become the largest photographic printing business in England. This image is part of the V&A's Francis Frith 'Universal Series' archive which consists of over 4000 whole-plate albumen prints predominantly of historical and topographical sites. Images such as these were highly desirable throughout the 1850s and 1860s. Frith's growing business coincided with many technological developments taking place within the field of photography. These developments changed and expanded the audience for photography and Frith's operation was well-prepared to provide for it and, it can be argued, worked to develop it employing a diverse range of publishing channels.
49fa2453-a0f1-50d3-9c2e-b116b3fe9fdd.author: Victoria and Albert Museum

4b55c559-2654-5a6f-a502-72a32dfa2c6a.name: Photo of the Aswan Railways inauguration
4b55c559-2654-5a6f-a502-72a32dfa2c6a.short_description: The inauguration of the Aswan Train Station, with `Adli Yakan Pasha; Muhammad Najib al-Gharabli Pasha; Husayn Rushdi Pasha; Tharwat Pasha; Fathallah Barakat Pasha; Morkos Hanna Pasha; al-Dagwi Bek, director of Aswan; and Mahmud Shakir Bek, deputy undersecretary of the Ministry of Transportation in attendance. The Egyptian railway line was the first to be established in Africa and the Middle East, and the second worldwide after the United Kingdom. The establishment of the first railway line in Egypt began on 12 June 1851, and it became operable in 1854. The Egyptian railway construction project supervisor at that time was British engineer Robert Stephenson, son of the famous inventor of locomotives, George Stephenson. The Aswan train station is one of the most important railway lines constructed during the reign of King Fu`ad.
keywords: Egyptian Railways; Aswan Railway Line; Transportation in Egypt

4b722a97-03c6-569f-b940-b4b7d60e5867.name: Photograph of Muhammad ‘Ali in *ihram* clothes during his pilgrimage of 1972
4b722a97-03c6-569f-b940-b4b7d60e5867.short_description:
This photograph was taken during Muhammad ‘Ali’s Hajj of January 1972. It was licenced by the United Press International (UPI) agency and dated 1/4/72, UPI sold its photo library during the 1960’s.  
The caption states:  
‘*Ali the pilgrim. Mecca, Saudi Arabia: Clad in a white robe and flanked by fellow-pilgrims, Muhamad Ali (center), the former Cassius Clay, prays inside the Holy Mosque in Mecca during his New Year’s pilgrimage to the Sanctum of the Moslem world. The ex-world champion appealed to the public to never call him by his former name again. He also said that after visiting the prophet’s tomb in Medina he became convinced that he can defeat Joe Frazier, the ruling boxing heavyweight world champ.*’
4b722a97-03c6-569f-b940-b4b7d60e5867.holder: Khalili Family Trust – Hajj and the Arts of Pilgrimage Collection
4b722a97-03c6-569f-b940-b4b7d60e5867.provenance: Shot in Mecca, probably printed in America
4b722a97-03c6-569f-b940-b4b7d60e5867.author: Qaisra Khan

4be86fc9-7fe9-524a-8ea0-665de458829d.name: The Italian woman poet and peace activist of Armenian descent Vittoria Aganoor Pompilj (1855–1910), and a signed copy of her poem 'Peace'
4be86fc9-7fe9-524a-8ea0-665de458829d.short_description: The descendant of an Armenian family that migrated to Venice at the beginning of the 19th century, Vittoria Aganoor Pompilj authored poems that were translated during her life into English, French and Spanish. She corresponded with many international literary figures and was a member of the International Arbitration and Peace League of Perugia (*Società per la pace e l'arbitrato internazionale di Perugia*), founded in 1892. In 1870, the British trade unionist Randal Cremer (Nobel peace laureate in 1907) founded the International Arbitration League, which –among other things – protested British intervention in Egypt and imperialism.
4be86fc9-7fe9-524a-8ea0-665de458829d.type: Photograph and autograph collected in a register
4be86fc9-7fe9-524a-8ea0-665de458829d.author: Maria Grazia Bistoni, Costanza Maria Del Giudice

4c12bb09-5654-50d7-9357-afc588c0f91d.name: Photograph of the dam of Sennar (Upper-Egypt) during its construction in April 1925
4c12bb09-5654-50d7-9357-afc588c0f91d.short_description: Since antiquity, those living around the Nile had attempted to take advantage of the floods to better irrigate their lands. Many dams were built in the 20th century, most notably at Aswan (1902). The first Sudanese dam was built in 1925, in Sennar in the Blue Nile state, in order to irrigate the agricultural region of Gezira.
keywords: Irrigation; dams; Egypt

4c22f475-8576-51f3-bde0-fc0eadf0e0ec.name: Italian Company Westinghouse. Factory at Vado Ligure [Genoa, Italy]. The Production of Ogives for Shells
4c22f475-8576-51f3-bde0-fc0eadf0e0ec.short_description:
Women working in an Italian factory that produced military equipment, during WWI. The war had an important impact on women’s work. As historian Perry Willson pointed out, during WWI “women rarely directly substituted for men, instead tending to move into new work roles produced by wartime expansion.”  
In Italy, the number of women who worked in factory producing weapons and ammunitions rose from 23,000 in 1915 to 198,000 in 1918. The numbers were far less than the women who participated in war production with more traditional “female roles”, such as making uniforms (400,000) or knitting woolen garments for the soldiers (200,000). However, Willson explained, women working in weapons’ factories had a relevance “as symbolic harbinger of change that greatly outweighed their actual numbers.”
4c22f475-8576-51f3-bde0-fc0eadf0e0ec.author: Cristina Mosillo, Giulia Barrera

4c5ec9e7-571c-57c0-a345-64717d007c10.name: *Nazareth School*
4c5ec9e7-571c-57c0-a345-64717d007c10.short_description: Pictured here is the Nazareth School, founded in 1868 by Mother Pauline de Vaux, Superior General of the Congregation of the Ladies of Nazareth. The decision to found this school was supported by the Bishop Vallegra, in Rome. It was first located in a large house in the European quarter of Beirut, nicknamed "The Blue Castle". However, with the number of students rapidly growing, the school had to relocate. In 1877 the new convent was opened for this purpose on St. George Hill, bought by the *firman* of Constantinople. The building is U-shaped and made of stone, with white cloisters and surrounded by a huge garden.
4c5ec9e7-571c-57c0-a345-64717d007c10.author: Hady El Hajj, Jennifer Harb, Cynthia Karaki
keywords: School; Education; Nazareth; Beirut

4c5f8ec8-becc-59f0-937c-3cc5e1969665.name: The digging of the Western Canal of the Aswan Dam
4c5f8ec8-becc-59f0-937c-3cc5e1969665.short_description:
Hundreds of Egyptian labourers digging the western canal of the Aswan Dam.  
Located in Upper Egypt, the Aswan Dam was the first water storage project in modern times.
keywords: Aswan Dam; Digging; Laborers; Labor

4cb14496-4bb6-5ace-9b66-d5e561825dc3.name: Antonio del Valle y Serrano, Marquis of Villa-Huerta
4cb14496-4bb6-5ace-9b66-d5e561825dc3.description: The Marquis of Cerralbo and his family visited Istanbul in 1889, and nowadays the Cerralbo Museum holds an interesting variety of pieces bought and collected as souvenirs from the family trip. When visiting a foreign country or city, being portraited by a famous photographer of studio was indispensable. In this case the photographers are the world-renowned Armenian Abdullah Frères, Photographes de S. M. I. le Sultan. This vignetted bust shot albumen portrait shows the elegance and the character of Antonio del Valle y Serrano, marquis of Villa-Huerta and stepson of the marquis of Cerralbo.
4cb14496-4bb6-5ace-9b66-d5e561825dc3.author: Cecilia Casas Desantes
keywords: Portrait; souvenir; memorabilia

4dcb750e-6c2b-5848-924b-43fb6905059d.name: Memorial Volume – Dedicatory and opening ceremonies of the Chicago World's Colombian Exposition – 1893
4dcb750e-6c2b-5848-924b-43fb6905059d.short_description: The World's Columbian Exposition or The Chicago World's Fair was a World's Fair held in Chicago in 1893 to celebrate the 400th anniversary of Christopher Columbus' arrival in the New World in 1492. The fair was an influential social and cultural event to which the Ottoman Empire had been invited. It displayed raw materials and agricultural products at the exposition, as well as handicraft products and plant products belonging to the palace revenue. The 1893 Chicago Exhibition was a big success for the Chamber of Commerce. The Head of the Chamber of Commerce, Azaryan Efendi, was assigned to the head of the commission, which was formed in Istanbul for the Chicago Exhibition.
keywords: International Exhibitions; exposition; fair

4df535c3-b510-5c68-a479-e3f13cd24179.name: Morocco. Irrigation channels in Marzuga
4df535c3-b510-5c68-a479-e3f13cd24179.description: The irrigation channels of Morocco, locally known as khettaras, are predominantly located in the southern areas of the country, on the margins of the Sahara Desert. Isolated oases, such as Merzouga, have relied on the khettaras for irrigation and survival since the 14th century AD. Functioning similarly to the aflaj of Oman, they work by drawing groundwater from areas of higher altitude to oases via underground tunnels that can be several kilometres long. In these images, we see them in use in local contexts, with water arriving to the village to irrigate the land.
4df535c3-b510-5c68-a479-e3f13cd24179.author: Yelyzaveta Basysta
keywords: Water; irrigation system; Merzouga; Morocco.

4ec3aa30-6ba0-5917-9e79-014b48d5cd78.name: *Giza – Austrian Headquarters*
4ec3aa30-6ba0-5917-9e79-014b48d5cd78.short_description: Picture of the Austrian research headquarters in Giza. The German-born Egyptologist Hermann Junker became a professor at the University of Vienna in 1909. In 1911 the Austrian Academy obtained the concession for excavation in Giza. In 1912 Hermann Junker's team started to excavate tombs close to the pyramids of Giza.
keywords: Hermann Junker; Egypt; Giza

4fba9c3c-f84d-510f-bba6-f6a6783a23b3.name: Nusretiye Mosque and the Imperial Gun Foundry in Tophane
4fba9c3c-f84d-510f-bba6-f6a6783a23b3.short_description: A frequently employed device in Robertson's Istanbul photographs is the inclusion of the one or more human figures in the foreground – indeed, this is something of a trademark of Robertson’s work. There were two main reasons for the inclusion of these figures. For one thing, the artist used them as a way of creating a more natural scene. The other was to provide one or more reference points so that the photograph’s viewers could get an idea of the dimensions of the scene they were looking at and of the elements contained therein.
4fba9c3c-f84d-510f-bba6-f6a6783a23b3.author: Bahattin Öztuncay
keywords: Istanbul photography; Ottoman architecture

5034d37c-081e-5b69-8d00-457af42ac16a.name: El Sayyid Muhammad Idris al-Mahdi al Senussi (1889–1983), from 1916 Chief of the Senussi Muslim order
5034d37c-081e-5b69-8d00-457af42ac16a.short_description: El Sayyid (or Sidi) Muhammad Idris al-Mahdi al Senussi (1889-1983), the grandson of the founder of the Senussi Sufi order, became head of the Senussi order in 1916. He took the title of Emir and ruled as King of Libya from 1951 through 1969. In 1920 Italy reached an agreement with him and invited him to Rome, where he met King Victor Emmanuel III. Idris’ relations with the Italian government later deteriorated, and he went into exile in Egypt and encouraged anti-Italian guerrilla from there.
5034d37c-081e-5b69-8d00-457af42ac16a.holder: Italian Institute for African and Oriental Studies
5034d37c-081e-5b69-8d00-457af42ac16a.author: Giulia Barrera

503f7b59-beb0-5c06-8952-0baa809cc018.name: *The arrival of the refugees*
503f7b59-beb0-5c06-8952-0baa809cc018.short_description:
A black and white photo from an album depicting the arrival of Greek refugees after the Asia Minor catastrophe. Photographer unknown.  
The “Convention concerning the exchange of Greek and Turkish population" was signed at Lausanne, on 30 January 1923, by the two governments. It involved approximately 2 million people (around 1.5 million Anatolian and 500,000 Muslims in Greece), most of whom were forcibly made refugees.
503f7b59-beb0-5c06-8952-0baa809cc018.author: Maria Dimitriadou
keywords: photo; refugees

523087c9-9a15-54a0-b37b-745c43c2cb51.name: An olive oil factory run by an Italian migrant in Monastir (Tunisia)

5296fe8d-c29c-5ac6-9be6-323c7b48cdf1.name: Fleeing the barbarians on the road to Amiens
5296fe8d-c29c-5ac6-9be6-323c7b48cdf1.short_description: Around 700,000 French citizens fled the country in the face of the German invasion at the beginning of the First World War (Spring 1914–1915). 532b4aae-3420-5fef-ba89-4653325f00d7.name: *A young and an old Turk*
532b4aae-3420-5fef-ba89-4653325f00d7.short_description: Carol Popp de Szathmari was born in Transylvania, but later settled in Bucharest, Wallachia, where he worked as court painter of princes Alexandru Dimitrie Ghica, Gheorghe Bibescu and Alexandru Ioan Cuza. During the reign of prince Carol of Hohenzollern, he was also court photographer. He is the author of five photographic albums with images of people and places from Bucharest and other regions in Romania, among which there are depictions of people belonging to the ethnic minorities of Romania, such as the Turks. He travelled twice to Istanbul, in 1860 and 1864, as member of prince Alexandru Ioan Cuza’s suite. During the Crimean War (1854-1855) he photographed the Russian and Turkish armies that occupied Wallachia and then went to Crimea, where he took more than 200 photos of the fights.

5417f6b5-cc8c-53f1-96de-52e25282f580.name: An Egyptian woman giving a public speech during the events of the 1919 Revolution
5417f6b5-cc8c-53f1-96de-52e25282f580.short_description: An Egyptian woman talking to the crowds, encouraging them to fight for their rights. The 1919 Revolution – one of the most important Egyptian revolutions in modern times– started due to objections to the practices of the British occupation and the exile of symbols of Egyptian patriotism.

547b1024-4367-52b2-8fb3-a58228f14a14.name: La Gare de Hidjaz, Damas (The Hijaz Station, Damascus)
547b1024-4367-52b2-8fb3-a58228f14a14.description: The Hijaz Railway Station was designed by the Spanish architect Fernando de Aranda (1878–1969). Raised at the Ottoman court in Istanbul, where his father directed the Imperial Military Band, Aranda settled permanently in Damascus following the deposition of Sultan Abdülhamid II in 1909. The station was designed within the broader Hijaz Railway project directed by Heinrich August Meissner Pasha (1862–1940), the German civil engineer and Chief Engineer of the Hijaz Railway. Although Aranda never obtained formal architectural qualifications and could not officially sign his projects, he became one of Damascus's most influential architects, designing the Hijaz Railway Station alongside numerous public and private buildings that shaped the city's early twentieth-century urban landscape.

54f861aa-1d28-5c1b-b3c3-07e65ff10862.name: 'Picture of the Tents of the Turks'. Photographer: H. A. Mirza & Sons
54f861aa-1d28-5c1b-b3c3-07e65ff10862.description:
This image shows the tents of the Ottoman Turkish troops at their camp at Medina. Despite the apparently secular nature of the subject, and the fact that the camp does not depict a stopping-off point on the hadj, the laudatory poetry and prose makes clear the relevance of the image to the experience of the hadj – that is, that the Turks, as ‘military people of the highest rank’ serve Islam by defending and enabling the passage to Mecca and Medina for other Muslims.  
  
As with the other photographs in this album (Photo 174/1-13), whose subjects are architectural and landscape, the figures are not the subject of the image. However, a detailed examination of the image shows the soldiers going about their day-to-day activities, such as cooking and eating. The method by which the ground would have been prepared before a tent was erected is indicated by the empty low circular foundation in the lower left corner of the image. In the distance, in the right-hand background of the image, beyond the dry-stone wall delineating the camp, palm groves and permanent dwellings can be identified.
54f861aa-1d28-5c1b-b3c3-07e65ff10862.dimensions: Mount (external): 35 x 44,6 cm; Mount (internal): 20,2 x 27,3 cm [landscape]
keywords: Travel; Hijaz; Medina; Mecca
materials: Mottled blue-tinted window mount, card, gelatin silver print, indigo ink (printed), red ink (hand-painted)

55817e68-2681-5c06-a3a1-71fdbd06edc2.name: Photograph of a diplomatic visit to England
55817e68-2681-5c06-a3a1-71fdbd06edc2.description: This photograph depicts the diplomatic delegation that accompanied Sultan of Morocco Mulay al-Hasan I’s Ambassador Hajj Muhammad al-Zebdi on an official visit to Britain at the invitation of Queen Victoria.

56672473-1926-594f-b790-6b908f455bae.name: Postcard published by Dimitri Tarazi & Fils. Beyrouth, Damas, Jérusalem (Postcard published by Dmimitri Tarazi and Sons, Beirut, Damascus, Jerusalem)
56672473-1926-594f-b790-6b908f455bae.description: The Mahmal al-Sharif and the Sanjak are the principal ceremonial symbols of the annual Syrian Hajj caravan departing from Damascus. The Mahmal was an elaborately embroidered ceremonial palanquin carried on a specially selected camel, and the Sanjak was the related banner. The tradition started during the Mamluk period and was later adopted by the Ottoman sultans as a symbol of their patronage of the pilgrimage and their role as Servants of the Two Holy Sanctuaries. A study by Behrens-Abouseif associated its origin with a legend related to the female Mamluk ruler, Shajarat al-Durr. The legend reflects the prominent participation of elite Mamluk women in pilgrimage and the exceptional political memory of Shajarat al-Durr as the first female ruler of the Mamluk Sultanate. For the people of Damascus, the Mahmal's departure and return were among the city's greatest religious and civic celebrations, drawing pilgrims, officials and large crowds into public processions that expressed communal participation in the Hajj.
56672473-1926-594f-b790-6b908f455bae.bibliography:

keywords: Hajj; pilgrimage; Damascus; Mahmal al-Sharif; Sanjak; Hajj caravan

56ae89a4-e69e-5467-915e-b99f5b5f752d.name: Panorama: al-hujjaj bi-mina yawn al-‘id al-akbar (‘The pilgrims at Mina on the day of the big feast’)
56ae89a4-e69e-5467-915e-b99f5b5f752d.description: Muhammad Sadiq Bey was the first person to take photographs of Mecca, Medina and the Hajj. An Egyptian army engineer and surveyor, he was also the treasurer of the Egyptian Hajj caravan, travelling numerous times to the Hijaz. Using a technique first invented in the 1850s, Sadiq Bey took his first photographs in 1861 using glass plate negatives, especially useful for large-format frames. His most important photographs, of both the buildings and interiors of the sanctuaries at Mecca and Medina, as well as sites at Arafat and Mina, were taken in 1861, 1880 and 1881. For the first time, the pilgrimage and the holy cities were precisely and realistically documented.
56ae89a4-e69e-5467-915e-b99f5b5f752d.holder: Khalili Family Trust – Hajj and the Arts of Pilgrimage Collection
keywords: Pilgrimage; Mina; Ottoman; Documentation; Photography;

56f05326-4b1d-5eff-9a58-a822374155ee.name: Portrait Of Binjamin Uziyel
56f05326-4b1d-5eff-9a58-a822374155ee.short_description: In 1911, when the Ottomans had to leave Tripoli, Binjamin Uziyel, who served in the consulate there, did research on a project of setting up sugar factories in Turkey after going to Genoa. He presented it to the Istanbul Chamber of Commerce by preparing a detailed report about setting up sugar factories in Turkey and ways to use the sugar beet.
56f05326-4b1d-5eff-9a58-a822374155ee.holder: The Quincentennial Foundation Museum, Archive of Turkish Jews
keywords: Jewish community in Istanbul in 19th century; trade; sugar; commodities; markets

578a0774-be4c-5eb0-85a3-86bf64c69e71.name: Palais du Bardo
578a0774-be4c-5eb0-85a3-86bf64c69e71.short_description: This postcard shows the throne room of the Palais du Bardo, with its rich furnishings and monumental chandeliers hanging from the ceiling. The bey's throne sits in the centre, surrounded by paintings of the princes of the Husainid dynasty, painted wooden ceilings, mirrors and console tables carved and painted with gold leaf, and with two great rooms on either side. From the 18th century onwards the Husainid beys continuously expanded and decorated the Palais du Bardo. The architecture and furniture all indicate a strong European, particularly Italian, influence.
578a0774-be4c-5eb0-85a3-86bf64c69e71.author: Saloua Khadhar Zangar
keywords: Palais du Bardo; beylical throne; European influences; Italian influences

579a1e8e-d0d1-5139-bb97-214a66f11b68.name: The Ottoman Navy, Mahmudiye
579a1e8e-d0d1-5139-bb97-214a66f11b68.short_description: The 19th century saw further decline in Ottoman naval power, despite occasional recovery. Following the defeat against the combined British-French-Russian fleet at the Battle of Navarino in 1827, Sultan Mahmud II gave priority to developing a strong and modern Ottoman naval force. The first steam ships of the Ottoman Navy were acquired in 1828. The ship of the line Mahmudiye, which had 128 cannons on three decks and carried 1,280 sailors on board, was built for the Ottoman Navy at the Imperial Naval Arsenal (Tersâne-i Âmire) on the Golden Horn in Constantinople.
579a1e8e-d0d1-5139-bb97-214a66f11b68.holder: Istanbul University, Nadir Eserler Kütüphanesi (Rare Books Library)
keywords: Yıldız Album; II. Abdulhamid Han; Photograph; Ottoman navy; Mahmudiye

5826ee6c-332d-51dd-951d-29eaf007b54d.name: Photograph of the *Sitara* and *Hizam* of the Ka‘ba of 1916
5826ee6c-332d-51dd-951d-29eaf007b54d.short_description: Following the outbreak of the First World War, and fearing that Egypt may not be able to send the customary *kiswa* for the *Ka‘ba*, one was made in Istanbul and sent to Mecca in AH 1334 / AD 1916, although it was not used until AH 1341 / AD 1922. The *sitara* and the eight panels that from the *hizam* are shown here displayed in the workshop where they were embroidered. Both bear the name of the Ottoman Sultan Mehmed V.

5873b7f8-20de-5178-a5f8-4103250abc6c.name: Bedouin women waiting to draw their ration of water.  Beni Selah, South Palestine. July 1917
5873b7f8-20de-5178-a5f8-4103250abc6c.description: A very long queue, mainly of Bedouin women, waiting to collect water rations in an open area with domestic buildings behind. To the left are two mounted Allied soldiers. There is a third mounted soldier facing the line of women on the right. The Allied troops are supervising the collection of water.

58837723-b1a0-5787-a2b8-812f79e409c5.name: Dr Charles Nicolle, Nobel Laureate for Medicine
58837723-b1a0-5787-a2b8-812f79e409c5.short_description: This is a photograph of Dr Charles Nicolle carrying out child vaccination on the indigenous Tunisian population. During his time at l'Institut Pasteur (1903–1936) he worked to prevent or eradicate infectious illnesses

58a491a4-71cc-5b24-a1a9-764a71488439.name: *Works for the opening of the Corinth Canal*
58a491a4-71cc-5b24-a1a9-764a71488439.short_description:
The Corinth Canal being dug. Photographer unknown.  
The Corinth Canal separates the Peloponnesian peninsula from the Greek. The idea of the canal was revived after Greece gained independence but soon abandoned due to economical reasons. The opening of the Suez Canal in 1869 gave an new impetus and the following year, the Zaimis government passed a law authorising the construction of the canal, which was formally inaugurated on 23 April 1882. Zaimis assigned the project to the Hungarian István Türr who set up the Société Internationale du Canal Maritime de Corinthe but the company failed and the project was finished by the company of Andeas Syngros. The canal was designed by the Hungarian engineer Béla Gerster with the assistance of the French Vincent Dauzants, a chief engineer of the Suez canal.

The chimney and the engine room of the water reservoir of Barbadinhos can be seen on the right side of the picture. The steam station was in operation until 1928, when a new electrically powered station was opened. After decommissioning, the machines were not dismantled and are currently preserved. The building of the Barbadinhos steam pumping station houses the Water Museum (opened in 1987) and was classified in 2010 as a building of public interest.

5bdaed42-778f-5c44-bbc4-20cefe2c165b.name: Retaining wall of the reservoir in Shellal, Egypt

He took several photographs of the works and of the monuments on the island of Philae that were slated to be submerged by the water. He published some of them in the *Bulletin of the Italian Geographical Society*, where he wrote that up to 2,000 Italian workers were employed in the works (as stone-cutters, miners and masons), out of a total labour force of about 10,000 or 12,000; an Italian village had sprung up on the Nile banks, with modest little houses, trattorias and shops.

It was inaugurated during the time of King Faruq, the son of King Fu`ad, and houses a large number of collections related to agricultural and rural environments, as well as agricultural plants and animals.

5c7df1fd-3c74-5952-b9c6-f24375461c19.name: *The Egyptian University – Faculty of Medicine*
5c7df1fd-3c74-5952-b9c6-f24375461c19.short_description:
General view of the Egyptian University Faculty of Medicine and Qasr al-\`Ayni Hospital in 1933.  
The 1923 Constitution stipulated that “Primary education is mandatory for all Egyptian boys and girls”. A decree was issued for the establishment of a public university under the name “The Egyptian University” in 1925, comprised of four faculties; literature, science, medicine and law. The Faculty of Medicine, annexed to Qasr al-\`Ayni Hospital, is one of the leading hospitals in the Arab World.

5ce76956-57f6-57ef-9da7-fc2a688258ea.short_description: Beylerbeyi Palace was commissioned by Sultan Abdülaziz (1830-76) and built between 1861 and 1865 as a summer residence and a place to entertain visiting heads of state. The Palace was designed by Sarkis Balyan in the second Empire. It looks its most attractive from the Bosporus, from which its two bathing pavilions – one for the *harem* (women's only) and the other for the *selamlik* (men's only) – can best be seen. One of the most attractive rooms is the reception hall, which has a pool and fountain. Running water was popular in Ottoman houses for its pleasant sound and cooling effect in the heat.

5dc4fbc5-e8e9-52ae-aa62-690ee8359b41.name: Lake d'Orta. Villa Crespi
5dc4fbc5-e8e9-52ae-aa62-690ee8359b41.short_description:
Cristoforo Benigno Crespi was a successful businessman active in the cotton industry. In 1879, he bought an estate near the lake d’Orta (Piedmont, Northern Italy), in order to build a vacation house in honour of his wife, Pia Travelli.  
He had fallen in love with the architecture of Baghdad, where he went to buy cotton, and asked architect Angelo Colla to build a villa in the Moorish style. Architect Enrico Combi designed the magnificent park.  
The villa features a 48-meter high minaret and has richly decorated interiors, made with marbles of great value, imported from several different countries. It required 12 year of works to be completed. The estate comprises a greenhouse, a wet dock, stables, a big fountain, an annex, and is surrounded by walls, with valuable wrought iron gates.
5dc4fbc5-e8e9-52ae-aa62-690ee8359b41.author: Ignazio Galella

5e05c455-44c3-5bd3-be12-061bbab9de8d.name: Musée de Cherchell. Fragments found in the excavations.
5e05c455-44c3-5bd3-be12-061bbab9de8d.short_description: The French established two museums in Algeria after the conquest: one in Algiers (1838), and another in Cherchell (1840). The latter was overshadowed by the reputation of the former and lacked subsidies. A report from 1855 describes abandoned collections, to which the objects found during an 1856 excavation were soon added. This image, dating from 1856, highlights both the richness of the works presented to the Musée de Cherchell and their inadequate conservation. A new museum, built in 1908, allowed the collections to be stored in better conditions.

60125102-5ebb-5175-b8f6-33c1bd1dcafc.name: Le Port, Vue générale, Les Douanes et la Gare de D.H.P. Beyrouth (Syria) (The Port Overview, Customs and the DHP StationBeirut, Syria).
60125102-5ebb-5175-b8f6-33c1bd1dcafc.description: Beirut Port was part of an integrated maritime and railway complex and the printed title of this postcard specifically identifies the customs facilities and the D.H.P. station. The train tracks run directly along the quay beside warehouses, illustrating the physical connection between maritime shipping and inland railway transport. The railway connection to the Beirut quay, completed in 1903, was intended to facilitate the direct movement of merchandise and reduce intermediate transhipment. The port infrastructure can be placed within the much larger transformation of Eastern Mediterranean commerce, with the nineteenth-century increase in Ottoman-European trade.

6195ae0a-159f-55a5-b0c8-2cb302571e83.name: Photo of al-Busiri Mosque
6195ae0a-159f-55a5-b0c8-2cb302571e83.short_description: The al-Busiri Mosque was named after the great Imam, famous for writing Sufi poetry about the love of God and in praise of his Prophet Muhammad. The fame of his poem “al-Burda” surpasses that of its writer. The mosque is located in Alexandria, in the Anfushi area in the Gomrok (al-Jumruk) district overlooking the Eastern Harbour, on the *Midan Al-Masajid* (The Square of Mosques). The Square of Mosques is so-named because the area is comprised of a large number of shrines to *Awliya’ Allah* (good people of God), who came to Alexandria during the Ayyubid and Mamluk times. The mosque consists of two separate squares: the mosque courtyard with a water fountain in the middle, surrounded by corridors from all directions; and the second square with the *qibla* wall or *iwan al-qibla*, which leads to the tomb of Imam al-Busiri. Above the tomb is a metal dome and the minaret which takes the shape of an obelisk. The dome and the minaret are in the 19th-century Turkish style.

61eb1293-6209-599c-bd83-34f180e3bec2.name: *The Port of Constanţa*
61eb1293-6209-599c-bd83-34f180e3bec2.short_description: The Black Sea port of Constanța underwent its first modernization while Dobruja, the province where it is situated, was under Ottoman control. In 1857, when the Ottoman government hired a British company to build a railway in Dobruja, the concluded contract also stipulated the reconstruction of the Constanța port. Completed in 1864, it was still a small harbor with a wooden dock, a dam and one cereals depot. After Dobruja was annexed by Romania, a law was issued in 1885 for the “improvement and augmentation” of the port. In 1896 its modernization was leased to a French enterprise but due to some disagreements, three years later the state took over the works, which were led by architect Anghel Saligny. Inaugurated in 1909, the new port had 3 dams, several docks, depots, silos, an oil basin, an electric plant.

6215ebc8-8b3b-5484-8ac2-a702cc00efad.name: Carol I, King of Romania (1839–1914) / Karl von Hohenzollern-Sigmaringen
6215ebc8-8b3b-5484-8ac2-a702cc00efad.short_description: Portrait of Carol I, King of Romania (1839–1914) on horseback/ Karl von Hohenzollern-Sigmaringen. He was elected Prince of Romania on the recommendation of Napoleon III in 1866. In 1881, after achieving formal independence from the Ottoman Empire, Carol declared himself King of Romania.

628ff64b-bf4e-573e-86cb-55190cee5fba.name: Water women 1/5
628ff64b-bf4e-573e-86cb-55190cee5fba.description: The photograph, entitled *Water Women* (2016), is a striking work from the Jordan National Gallery of Fine Arts that fuses portraiture, landscape and cultural symbolism into a multilayered visual narrative. By employing the technique of double exposure, the artist superimposes an image of a smiling woman carrying a water container on her head upon the typically rugged sandstone terrain and ancient steps that are characteristic of Petra. This merging of human and environment transforms the subject into a living embodiment of endurance and heritage, connecting the labour of daily survival with the monumental legacy of Jordan's desert civilisation. The photograph is indicative of themes of resilience, gender and ecology. The subject's countenance, characterised by a poised yet radiant expression, serves to create a pronounced visual contrast with the arid landscape, thereby underscoring the pivotal role women play in the sustenance of life in such inhospitable environments. The water jug positioned on her head functions as both a literal vessel of survival and a metaphorical burden, thereby echoing the carved steps and eroded stone, which are symbols of persistence and continuity through time. From a visual perspective, the warm ochres of the sandstone blend harmoniously with the cool tones of her embroidered clothing. This creates a dialogue between tradition and adaptation. The presence of an additional veiled woman, walking in the background and carrying bottled water, serves to anchor the image in contemporary realities of scarcity and modernity. Collectively, these elements form a layered composition that evokes a poetic meditation on the intersection of nature, culture and feminine strength. This work is situated within a broader discourse of Middle Eastern identity and environmental consciousness in modern photographic art.
628ff64b-bf4e-573e-86cb-55190cee5fba.holder: Jordan National Gallery of Fine Arts
keywords: woman; water; photograph; print

629911e6-06d2-536a-9acd-824991f44ffa.name: Ferdinand, King of Romania (1865–1927) / Ferdinand von Hohenzollern-Sigmaringen
629911e6-06d2-536a-9acd-824991f44ffa.short_description: Portrait of Ferdinand I, King of Romania. After the death of King Carol I, Ferdinand (as the nephew of the deceased king) ascended to the throne. In 1916 he joined the *entente* and declared war against Austria and Germany. After World War I, Romania gained Transylvania, Bukowina and the Banat from Austria, and Bessarabia from Russia. Ferdinand died in Romania in 1927.

63e03fb2-ff4b-5263-b342-f74d2b6bdf14.name: La Grande Gare du Hidjaz, Damas (The Grand Railway Station of Hijaz, Damascus)
63e03fb2-ff4b-5263-b342-f74d2b6bdf14.description: The Hijaz Railway Station building is one of several major public buildings established during the late Ottoman period under the rule of Sultan Abdülhamid II in Damascus. The construction was carried out under the supervision of Hüseyin Nazım Pasha, the Wali (Governor) of Damascus and chairman of the committee responsible for implementing the Hijaz Railway project. He oversaw the plan to construct the railway between Damascus and Medina from 1900 to 1908, mobilising conscripts and civilian labour to participate in its construction, while also benefiting from the expertise of German engineers and other foreign specialists who came to supervise the railway project.

640180dd-059b-54fe-a33c-0700c3dd70f8.name: Photograph of the Beirut–Aleppo railway
640180dd-059b-54fe-a33c-0700c3dd70f8.short_description: The second railway built in Lebanon opened in 1906 and ran from Beirut to Aleppo in present-day Syria. It connected with the first railway line at Riyaq. The connection between Aleppo and Beirut, a well-equipped and sizeable port, decreased trade in Alexandretta, the traditional port for merchandise leaving or entering Syria. Alexandretta was not connected to Aleppo by rail until 1914. Aleppo and Northern Syria became increasingly important as links between Damascus and Beirut were consolidated. This also marked the increasing importance of Beirut as a powerful city in the region and not only as a Mediterranean port.
640180dd-059b-54fe-a33c-0700c3dd70f8.author: Hady El Hajj, Jennifer Harb, Cynthia Karaki

6407ba69-5120-5550-9850-d55a3019a722.name: Railway construction works
6407ba69-5120-5550-9850-d55a3019a722.description: The Giaurdere Viaduct, its name during construction, is now known as the Varda Viaduct and was constructed near Hacıkırı in the Taurus Mountains. Built between 1907 and 1912 for the Baghdad Railway, the bridge follows a curved alignment across a deep ravine and rises about 99 metres above the valley floor over a length of roughly 172 metres. It was built by Philipp Holzmann A.G. Architecturally, the viaduct (long, high bridge with a series of arches) combines monumental stone-clad piers with three principal arches and shorter approach spans. The tall, lattice supports reduce the structure’s visual mass while carrying the railway deck high above the irregular terrain; the repeated arches create a strong, stable structure across the valley. The photograph also shows the temporary lower bridge, which was used as an alternative line until the finish of the construction and to transport stone, steel, workers and machinery before the permanent crossing could operate.

647bb6c0-14ae-506b-85c5-060226c34178.name: Poet Nigar Hanım
647bb6c0-14ae-506b-85c5-060226c34178.short_description: Nigar Hanım, who was born in Istanbul in 1856, studied in a French school. She also took private Turkish, Arabic and Persian classes. She started to write poems when she was a child. She had a very good command of the French language and French literature. Every Tuesday, she gathered reputable personalities at her place, where they discussed art and literature, listened to music and read poems. She collected her poems in *Efsûs I* (1877), *Efsûs II* (1891), *Nîram* (1896), *Aks-i Seda* (1900) and *Elhan-i Vatan* (1916). She also wrote a work of prose in 1901 entitled *Safahat-i Kalb*. A fine lyricism that expresses her unhappiness in her private life can be observed in her work. Among the Turkish poets, she was the most productive, writing very original pieces in the second half of the 19th century.

64991688-a812-5045-be71-b7c312480a11.short_description: The Black Obelisk became famous in 1850’s because it named two figures known from the Bible, and even depicted one of them. 64d43d8c-378d-5f7b-8572-8f2de200829a.short_description: The mobilisation of the German army in early August 1914 was quickly followed by the mobilisation of the French army. 65ab9cb8-2305-56ee-99fd-eb52c5bbaf5d.name: Valeria Mengarini Rossetti (the wife of an Italian military officer) visiting Menfi (Egypt), escorted by her brother-in-law Roberto Rossetti (an Italian lawyer who migrated to Egypt)
65ab9cb8-2305-56ee-99fd-eb52c5bbaf5d.short_description:
During the 19th century, the number of Europeans who could engage in leisure travel steadily increased, and tourism began to flourish. Ancient Egypt became an attractive tourist destination for the European elites. Fascination for Egyptian antiquities and the cultural exoticism were sources of interest.  
Near Egyptian ruins, tourist could also enjoy the exotic experience of riding a camel.

65c69c9e-9fa5-59d3-9011-708e7d931372.short_description: General view of the pyramids of Abusir, in the area of the pyramids of the king Userkaf and king Neferirkare. These pyramids represent vestiges of the Fifth Dynasty, and they date back to 2800 BC (Old Kingdom). The paper photograph is printed from glass plate negatives.

65d5d950-d069-5d9e-989f-ca9b3eb57b29.name: *Harem*
65d5d950-d069-5d9e-989f-ca9b3eb57b29.short_description: Pascal Sébah (1823–1886) was a French photographer working in the Ottoman Empire. This photo of a harem is interesting insofar as it  differs from the mainstream representations of harems in the Western imagination, which were influenced by the painter Gérôme. Indeed, many local customs - both real and imagined - captured the interest of European artists, and their Orientalist art then fuelled both the Western fascination with and revulsion towards the East.

6755e6c3-6bcf-5ff8-9576-394e0f98a7c5.name: Beginning of the Royal Road from the direction of the Fayum Directorate
6755e6c3-6bcf-5ff8-9576-394e0f98a7c5.short_description: The beginning of the royal road from the Fayum Directorate during King Fu`ad I’s visit to the Directorate on 8 May 1927. Fu`ad I ruled Egypt from 9 October 1917 to 28 April 1936. During his reign, the 1919 revolution began, and the British had to end Egypt's status as a protectorate and declare it an independent country with sovereignty. Independence was declared on 15 March 1922. Also during his reign, the first public ministry was established in January 1924, headed by Sa`d Zaghlul. King Fu`ad had a number of important accomplishments, and for this reason this photo was chosen – to manifest King Fu`ad's concern with roads, especially the royal road towards the Fayum Directorate.
keywords: King Fu`ad; Fayum Directorate; new roads; The Royal Road

679af2a1-a210-5f1f-927c-cd4ef3b1d0b4.name: Iron bridge near Haifa
679af2a1-a210-5f1f-927c-cd4ef3b1d0b4.description: This album of 39 images documents the construction of the Hijaz Railway. It photographs two important stretches of the network: the route between Damascus and Maʿan, and the line connecting Daraʿa with Haifa. Its photographs record the remarkable engineering achievements required to negotiate difficult and varied terrain, while also illustrating the railway’s role in strengthening connections across the empire. Alongside tunnels, bridges and stations, the images capture the engineers, officials and labourers whose work made the project possible.
679af2a1-a210-5f1f-927c-cd4ef3b1d0b4.holder: The Nasser D. Khalili Collection of Hajj and The Arts of Pilgrimage

6810a977-0fac-5c5e-a9a2-56e6c3bc3a3a.name: Italian and Tunisian miners at work
6810a977-0fac-5c5e-a9a2-56e6c3bc3a3a.short_description: According to the book where this photo was published, in 1906 the largest number of Italian miners in Tunisia worked in El Kef (2,000) and in Gafsa (1,200). The most important mineral resource in Tunisia were phosphates, but the country also had mines of copper, manganese, iron and lead. One could find Italian miners in all these mines.

68e8b7c1-4b26-5650-8465-4d55145c3d6c.name: *Convoy of pilgrims*
68e8b7c1-4b26-5650-8465-4d55145c3d6c.short_description: The Hijaz Railway was a narrow-gauge railway (1,050mm/​3ft, 5 11⁄32 in track gauge) that ran from Damascus to Medina, through the Hijaz region of Saudi Arabia, with a branch line to Haifa on the Mediterranean Sea. It was a part of the Ottoman railway network and was built to extend the line from the Haydarpaşa Terminal in Istanbul beyond Damascus to the holy city of Mecca. It got no further than Medina, 400 kilometres (250mi) short of Mecca, due to the construction interruption caused by the outbreak of World War I. The main purpose of the railway was to establish a connection between Constantinople, the capital of the Ottoman Empire and the seat of the Islamic Caliphate, and Hijaz in Arabia, the site of the holiest shrines of Islam and the holy city of Mecca, the destination of the Hajj (annual pilgrimage).

6918edf0-4e2e-58b2-82d5-437119b828fa.short_description: The Lycée Armand-Fallières, attended in his time by Jules Ferry and named after the President of the French Republic, was located on the Rue de Russie and had the objective of educating the daughters of European settlers in their secondary education. In the early 20th century, a few Tunisians began to attend the school and thus had access to a modern European education. This photograph shows a secondary school class of young girls.

6996faf2-9ef0-57f8-8ffd-b45d86af0d67.name: Third-grade pupils of the Italian state-funded Giovanni Meli primary school in Tunis
6996faf2-9ef0-57f8-8ffd-b45d86af0d67.short_description:
In 1831, siblings Pompeo and Ester Sulema, political refugees from Livorno, opened the first Italian school in Tunis. By the end of the 19th century, there were 21 Italian state schools in Tunisia: 13 in Tunis, three in La Goulette, three in Sousse and two in Sfax. Five of them were pre-schools, eleven were primary schools and five were secondary schools.  
The Italian State could run schools in Tunisia thanks to the treaty signed by Italy and Tunisia in 1868. In 1881, Tunisia became a French protectorate and in 1896 Italy and France signed a treaty over the status of Italians in Tunisia: the Italian state could continue to run schools in Tunisia but could not open new ones. So, classes became very crowded, as shown in this photo.
6996faf2-9ef0-57f8-8ffd-b45d86af0d67.author: Giulia Barrera

699fbe74-5142-545f-991c-73824a07527f.name: Author Tevfik Fikret and his book of poetry *Rübab-ı Şikeste*
699fbe74-5142-545f-991c-73824a07527f.short_description: Tevfik Fikret, who published his first book of poetry *Rubab-ı Şikeste* (broken instrument), dealt with love, piety, nature and a worldview that was self-enclosed to the environment. His poems influenced other Turkish poets and he is considered a pioneer of contemporary Turkish poetry. His work also has some seeds of the social opposition of the future.

69c68c59-f8ea-58f9-8d04-9f7f7e1327d4.name: In the Sicilian Sulphur Mines
69c68c59-f8ea-58f9-8d04-9f7f7e1327d4.short_description:
Sicilian sulphur mines at the end of the 19th century employed children as young as seven and eight years old to carry the crude ore up from the mines to the surface.  
In Italy, the first piece of law regarding children’s work dates back to 1886. It forbade employing children under the age of nine in factories and mines. It also dictated that children under the age of 12 could not work at night. Such provisions indicated the extremely hard situation of children workers at the time. Particularly appalling were the working conditions of children in the Sicilian sulphur mines. Their plight was highlighted by the Italian writer Giovanni Verga in his short story *Rosso Malpelo*, and by Nobel laureate Luigi Pirandello in his *Ciàula scopre la Luna*.
69c68c59-f8ea-58f9-8d04-9f7f7e1327d4.holder: State Library of Modern and Contemporary History
69c68c59-f8ea-58f9-8d04-9f7f7e1327d4.author: Giulia Barrera

69f1c95c-2875-58ff-b85b-10d1c2d2ab83.name: Marius Scalesi
69f1c95c-2875-58ff-b85b-10d1c2d2ab83.short_description: Pictured here is Marius (Mario) Scalesi, a young poet of Italian origin, born on 6 February 1892 in Tunis to an Italian father and a Maltese mother. He suffered from tuberculosis from birth, and became paralysed following a fall down the stairs in his home in La Goulette, the so-called "Little Sicily" of Tunis. Forced to abandon his studies in order to make a living, he completed his education independently. His articles of literary criticism and poems were published in the journal *La Tunisie Illustrée*. His collection of poems, *Les Poèmes d'un Maudit* sheds light on the hardships of his life. He died in 1922 in an asylum in Palermo. A fascinating figure due to his triple cultural identity - Italian, French and Tunisian - he is considered one of the pioneers of North African poetry in French.

6a3c68eb-7bea-5e92-8112-9d9d0c950351.name: The Bach Hamba brothers
6a3c68eb-7bea-5e92-8112-9d9d0c950351.short_description: 'Ali (pictured here) and Mohamed were two of the leaders of the protest movement "Harakat al-Shabab al-Tunisi" (the Young Tunisians). Born in Tunis in 1876 and 1881 respectively, these two men of Turkish origin helped found a French-language newspaper, *Le Tunisien*, through which they attacked the politics of the French colonialists and demanded reform. With the help of their comrades, the brothers organised many acts of resistance, such as the Jellaz Affair (1911) and the tramway boycott (1912). The arrest of the majority of the movement's founders, and the suppression of the newspaper *Le Tunisien* marked the end of their activities in Tunisia. However, they continued to make their demands from abroad, working mainly in Geneva and Istanbul, where they finally died in 1818 ('Ali) and 1820 (Mohamed).

6a89da25-5756-58bf-b49f-f4fde99fe13b.name: Istanbul Archaeological Museums
6a89da25-5756-58bf-b49f-f4fde99fe13b.short_description: In the 19th century, efforts were in place to modernize the Ottoman Empire, as many of the leading statesmen had been exposed to Westernizing ideas through education and travel. This museum was founded by decree as the Imperial Museum (*İmparatorluk Müzesi*) in 1891. The first curator and founder of the museum was Osman Hamdi Bey. Construction of the main building began in 1881, attaining its present neo-Greek form in 1908. The architect was Alexander Vallaury. The site of the museum belonged to the Topkapı Palace outer gardens. It is a prominent structure built in the neoclassical style in Istanbul.

6c4a7fd1-e659-525c-ad3d-c6180e7f9ebe.name: Palästina. Haifa. Panorama (Palestine)
6c4a7fd1-e659-525c-ad3d-c6180e7f9ebe.description: A panoramic view of Haifa’s coastline is shown in this postcard. The city developed into an important Mediterranean outlet of the Hijaz Railway after the construction of the Daraa–Haifa branch in the early twentieth century. Once the line connected the Syrian interior and the Hauran with the coast, Haifa gained a more important role in regional trade and transportation. Haifa Station and railway construction were part of a broader Ottoman programme of urban and infrastructural development in the city.

Alexander Vallaury, a French-Turkish architect living in the city designed the hotel in a blend of neo-classical, art nouveau and oriental styles. The hotel was the first building in Turkey to be powered by electricity other than the Ottoman Palaces. It was also the only address in the city to provide hot running water for its guests and was home to the first electric elevator in Istanbul.

6cd47255-25d3-54ce-a323-50d1b8890c29.name: La Gare du Hijaz, Damas (The Hijaz Railway Station, Damascus)
6cd47255-25d3-54ce-a323-50d1b8890c29.description: The Hijaz Station in Damascus, originally known locally as Qanawat Station, was originally built in 1903 and later became the main starting point of the Hijaz  Railway linking Damascus with Medina. In 1912, a competition was organised to select a new design for the Hijaz Station. As a result, the new building designed by the Spanish architect Fernando de Aranda was opened to the public in 1917. The design was a combination of historicism and Rococo, with local architectural elements like Ablaq and ornamentation like Ajami.

6faa2e57-f95c-52d9-a61f-402154b53322.name: Organ Made in Tunis by the Italian Firm Cesare Trionfo and Exhibited in Milan
6faa2e57-f95c-52d9-a61f-402154b53322.short_description:
Cesare Trionfo was a child when he migrated with his family to Tunisia from Livorno in 1855. He became a trader, and in 1886 he started trading musical instruments. In Tunis, he later also started a shop that made musical instruments such as this organ. Trionfo promoted the construction of the theatre Politeama Roissini, which he co-owned.  
This organ was exhibited in Milan for the 1906 international exhibition. The organ is a traditional Italian musical instrument. This one has decorative elements taken from Arab architecture.

The museum was founded by decree in 1891 as the Imperial Museum. The first curator and founder of the museum was Osman Hamdi. Hamdi began construction of the main building in 1881, and it achieved its present neo-Greek form in 1908. The architect was Alexander Vallaury. It is one of the prominent structures built in the neoclassical style in Istanbul. Osman Hamdi, during his tenure as museum director, launched the first Turkish scientific excavations. 713a80ee-86ad-5103-bcf7-5c70eb44eb3b.name: The interior of Tabuk Hospital
713a80ee-86ad-5103-bcf7-5c70eb44eb3b.short_description: In 1900 the Ottoman Sultan Abdülhamid II (r.1876–1909) began the construction of a railway line connecting Damascus to the holy cities of Medina and Mecca. Built by public subscription and with an appeal to Muslims of the world for financial support, the railway line reached Medina in 1908, but didn't reach Mecca. It was built with the assistance of German engineers who worked closely with Turkish officials. This album of the Hijaz Railway probably belonged to a Turkish engineer who worked on the construction of the line. It has 50 photographs, mostly of stations and sections of the line, but also of the landscape that the line passed through in the area between Tabuk and Mada’in Salih. The photographs were most likely taken by J. H. Halladjian, an Armenian photographer with a studio in Haifa in Palestine active in the 1890s and early 20th century. Based on records at the Imperial War Museum and The Royal Geographical Society, Halladjian took photographs of the Hijaz Railway and places along its route. The album contains some important photographs such as the one of the hospital at Tabuk which was established in 1907 and which became the railway’s quarantine station (ARC.al 6.16) as well as images which demonstrate the hardship of cutting through rock in order to pass the line through mountainous terrain (ARC.al 6.24). Also documented here are the great stone monoliths north of Mada'in Salih (ARC.al 6.38) in Mabrak al Naga, where prior to the Hijaz Railway, the Ottoman government connected the Hijaz to Istanbul via a telegraph line which reached Mada'in Salih in 1900. The building of the overland telegraph line between Damascus and Medina, much like the construction of the Hijaz Railway project to follow, was fraught with complications including the terrain and the danger of Bedouin resistance.

71d240aa-d335-59ff-8b64-aa4539d24c3b.name: *The Grand Mosque in Constanţa*
71d240aa-d335-59ff-8b64-aa4539d24c3b.short_description: The Grand Mosque of Constanţa, the biggest in Romania, was built between 1910–1913 for the Muslim community of the city, on the initiative of king Carol I. It was erected on the place of a 19th century mosque, whose minbar (pulpit from where the imam delivers sermons) was preserved. The monument, a mixture of Byzantine-Egyptian and Romanian architectural elements, is the work of architect Victor Ştefănescu, who before designing it travelled to Istanbul to get acquainted with Islamic architecture. The mosque was inaugurated on 31 May 1913 in the presence of Romania’s king and queen and of Romanian and Ottoman officials. The envoy of sultan Abdul Hamid II brought a Persian rug for the mosque and awarded the orders of “Medjidie” and “Osmanieh” to Victor Ştefănescu and the city’s may.

71d76fc5-c9ad-524d-9391-c2dd24da5ac5.name: Chemin de fer, Postcard, Alep (Aleppo Railway Station)
71d76fc5-c9ad-524d-9391-c2dd24da5ac5.description: This composite postcard presents Aleppo’s earlier railway complex, generally identified as Damascus Station, together with a separate building labelled Pavillon militaire. Located in the Jamiliyeh district of Aleppo, the station served the French-operated railway Damas, Hama et Prolongements (D.H.P.), linking Aleppo southward through Hama and Homs with Damascus. The Hama–Aleppo extension entered service in 1906. The upper image shows a restrained two-storey masonry station with a long covered platform, regularly spaced windows and numerous chimneys, reflecting its combined passenger, administrative and possibly staff functions. The lower image records the military pavilion, with a raised entrance, deep tiled roofs and an ornamental timber porch distinguish it from the station building.

7281683b-fda9-593c-917d-2afe6e08c7b6.name: Building a bridge near Haifa
7281683b-fda9-593c-917d-2afe6e08c7b6.description: This album of 39 images documents the construction of the Hijaz Railway. It photographs two important stretches of the network: the route between Damascus and Maʿan, and the line connecting Daraʿa with Haifa. Its photographs record the remarkable engineering achievements required to negotiate difficult and varied terrain, while also illustrating the railway’s role in strengthening connections across the empire. Alongside tunnels, bridges and stations, the images capture the engineers, officials and labourers whose work made the project possible.

742e675b-2783-5254-a6e4-abd2e2dc3cd3.name: *Monument commemorating the installation of the Hijaz-Damascus telegraph connection, Damascus*
742e675b-2783-5254-a6e4-abd2e2dc3cd3.short_description: This monument is a well-known benchmark, which remained the symbol of the municipal administration until a few years ago. The bronze column in the middle of the Merje Square was erected in commemoration of the Istanbul-Damascus-Mecca telegraph link. It was the line with the sultan’s Islamist policy, acting as a symbol of the Ottoman claim to leadership over Muslims. The monumental telegraph column is crowned by a model of the Istanbul Hamidiye Mosque, where every week the Sultan ‘Abdülhamid [`Abd al-Hamid II] had his visit to the mosque for Friday prayers celebrated with an imperial march-past- a demonstration of the concentrated political power of the Sultan.

74dafe7a-b3e7-5be6-b35d-e97ef0242008.name: The cruiser Bascir during a test voyage at sea
74dafe7a-b3e7-5be6-b35d-e97ef0242008.short_description:
In 1890, political pressure from Italian Prime Minister Francesco Crispi secured construction of the cruiser Bascir for the Moroccan Navy for the Fratelli Orlando shipyards located in Livorno (Italy), winning against French competitors.  
The Bascir was the first cruiser built by an Italian shipyard for a foreign navy after Italian unification in 1860. It was delivered to Morocco in 1894. Among its amenities was a hamam (in Western Europe often known as Turkish Bath), expressly requested by the buyer.  
The Fratelli Orlando shipyards also built a yacht for the Khédivé of Egypt.
74dafe7a-b3e7-5be6-b35d-e97ef0242008.author: Daniela Tazzi

752b7f53-4c79-5513-bbe6-c8c51b39c873.name: German Jildirim photocard
752b7f53-4c79-5513-bbe6-c8c51b39c873.description: The photographic postcard shows merchants with loaded camels alongside a railway freight yard. The scene documents an important commercial dimension of the Hijaz Railway. Alongside pilgrims and soldiers, the line transported merchandise between regional markets and contributed to increased economic and trading activity. Rail transport did not immediately replace camel caravans. Camels continued to bring agricultural produce and other loads from villages, pastoral areas and routes beyond the tracks to railway stations, where goods could be transferred to wagons for longer-distance shipment. Historians therefore describe animal transport as a feeder to the late Ottoman railway network rather than simply its outdated rival. During the First World War, this combined system became still more important, since trains carried bulk freight along fixed routes while camels supplied places beyond the railway. The seated men and water pipe also reveal the freight yard as a social space of waiting, work and exchange, bringing together traders, animal handlers and railway infrastructure.

75686fa8-f38a-5ba8-bc38-088996a3046a.name: Photographic postcard of Jannat al-Baqi‘, Medina
75686fa8-f38a-5ba8-bc38-088996a3046a.short_description: These photographic postcards when joined together form a panoramic view of al-Baqi‘ graveyard in Medina. Otherwise known as ‘*Baqi‘al-Gharqad*’ this graveyard is on the south-eastern side of the Prophet's Mosque and was a site chosen by the Prophet Muhammad as an exclusive Muslim cemetery. It is known as the oldest and most important historical Islamic graveyard. Many of the Prophet’s companions, family-members and followers are buried there. Although early travel accounts (for example, that of Ibn Jubayr (d. AD 1217)) state that the exact location of many graves had been lost, certainly until 1925, it was possible to locate many important early Muslim graves. For Shiˋa Muslims this is where four of the Shiˋi imams are buried, making it a special place of visitation. In this panoramic, the buildings which had been constructed over significant graves are identifiable. The larger building visible in ARC.pc 401 is the mausoleum the *Ahl al-bayt* (members of the Prophet’s family), while the smaller buildings were known to be the resting-places specifically of the wives and children of the Prophet. The buildings and tombstones no longer exist as they were destroyed by the Wahhabis under Ibn Saud in 1926. The original photographs were taken by a Turkish photographer for Bernhard Moritz, a Professor of Oriental Languages in Berlin, during his travels in the Middle East between 1905 and 1915. They were first published in *Bilder aus Palästina, Nord-Arabien und dem Sinai* (Images from Palestine, North Arabia, and the Sinai) which contains 105 photographs of the Middle East and published by Moritz in 1916.

75ba6380-c797-5b14-a144-d7546e1f3572.name: *Album de la Dobrudgea* by Anatol Magrin
75ba6380-c797-5b14-a144-d7546e1f3572.short_description: In 1878 Anatole Magrin was appointed secretary of the French consul to Constanța and then became vice-consul and consul. He married a Romanian woman and eventually settled in Constanța. He was the owner of the first photo studio in the city and later became the official photographer of king Carol I, who decorated him with the Romanian order of the Crown. He is considered to be the first artist to take photographs of Dobruja, a province in the south-east of Romania which was restored to Romania in 1878, after more than three centuries of Ottoman domination. Magrin’s photo album dedicated to Dobruja contains 56 photos of landscapes and people, some of which depict Turkish and Tatar communities (the Tatars and Turks represent one of Dobruja’s main ethnic minorities).

7625cc1a-04cd-541e-97b3-01fa3eac5fdf.short_description: Lacan heaps particular praise on the artist's panorama taken from Beyazıt Tower as well as on his photograph of the architectural elements of Galata Tower, the Hagia Sophia, the Mosque of Sultan Ahmed I, and Dolmabahçe Sarayı. Robertson’s Istanbul photographs are concerned primarily with the city’s historical monuments. They reveal the city’s magnificent Byzantine and Ottoman structures from different angles and with close-ups taken in an approach that is usually quite aesthetic.

76457a6e-00a0-52e0-a869-4eec84837b92.short_description: The first railroad in Macedonia was the track running from Thessalonica via Skopje to Belgrade. Its construction was financed with foreign investments and began in 1871. The track to Skopje was finished in 1873. The Skopje-Mitrovica railway line was completed in 1878.
