76a1492a-0881-5283-861f-8c45c2c06097.name: L'École de la Rue du Pacha (inside the classroom)
76a1492a-0881-5283-861f-8c45c2c06097.short_description: This photograph shows a classroom of young Muslim girls at l'École Louise-Renée-Millet (renamed l'École de la Rue du Pacha in 1911/1912) in 1908. The presence of a *moueddeb* and a French teacher is notable. The *moueddeb* would have taught the principles of the Quran and elementary Arabic (reading, writing, arithmetic), whereas the French teacher would have covered the French education (literature, history, science and hygiene), as well as needlework (embroidery, sewing, lace). For the younger pupils of the school this classroom was the door to the world and one which allowed them to explore life. Young girls of this time often lived very sheltered lives, shut away in their homes without the opportunity to learn. Their education was usually limited to housework and needlework, either at home or at a Dar el-Maalma, a local atelier run by an old housewife.

776b254f-37bf-5617-8d2b-3b37c80ca73f.name: San Remo: The Conference of the Four Nations
776b254f-37bf-5617-8d2b-3b37c80ca73f.description: San Remo Conference, April 1920. Held after World War I, this conference brought together Britain, France, Italy and Japan to decide the fate of former Ottoman lands. Britain received mandates over Palestine and Mesopotamia (later Iraq), while France gained Syria and Lebanon. Rooted in the Sykes–Picot plan and the Balfour Declaration, these decisions also determined the future of Ottoman infrastructure such as the Hijaz Railway. Strikingly, no representatives from the region were present and the map of the Middle East was redrawn without local voices.

77f52d4b-ff6b-552e-acdb-df8edbe68721.name: Ismail, Khedive of Egypt (1830–1895)
77f52d4b-ff6b-552e-acdb-df8edbe68721.short_description: Portrait of Ismail, Khedive of Egypt (1830–1895), who financed the construction of the Suez Canal. Because of the enormous costs of the building and his reform measures, Egypt's debt rose from three million pounds sterling to 100 million pounds sterling. In 1875 Egypt was bankrupt and Ismail Pasha was forced to sell 176,602 shares to Great Britain for 3,976,582 pounds sterling. Egypt came under financial control of France and Great Britain.
keywords: Ismail, Khedive of Egypt; Suez Channel; Emperor Franz Joseph

77f7d1f5-f298-526e-8bfa-21c5a75d09f2.name: *4 June 1913, Gand, \[pavillion from\] the French Protectorate in Morocco \[Exposition Universelle et Internationale\]*
77f7d1f5-f298-526e-8bfa-21c5a75d09f2.short_description: In 1913, Gand (Belgium) hosted the 28th Exposition Universelle (world fair). Like France, Belgium gave pride of place to its colonies. During its universal expositions (world fairs), France tended to exhibit a number of colonial pavilions, whose architecture and "exoticism" fascinated visitors. The "Pavilion from the French Protectorate in Morocco" was built to show off the recent (1912) Moroccan protectorate.
keywords: Universal expositions; colonies; Morocco

78eecb65-6040-5c83-8995-b8c35cb4d3a6.name: Nusretiye Mosque and Tophane Square
78eecb65-6040-5c83-8995-b8c35cb4d3a6.short_description: James Robertson arrived in Istanbul in 1840 and started work as head etcher in Ottoman Mint. He began taking photos of Istanbul soon after. There was previously a mosque located on the site of the current Mosque, which was known as the Mosque of the Artillery Barracks (Tophane-i Amire Arabacilar Kislasi Camii) built by Selim III (1789-1807). When that mosque was destroyed by the Firuzaga fire, the Nusretiye Mosque, located on Meclis-i Mebusan Street in the Tophane District of Beyoglu, was built on the order of Sultan Mahmud (1784-1839), and was constructed by the Krikor Amira Balyan. The construction lasted from 1823 to 1826 and was broadly restored between the years of 1955 and 1958, and partially again between 1980 and 1992. While its architecture is influenced by Islamic elements, it retains a Baroque style, making it unique to the city.
keywords: Photograph; Old İstanbul Photograph; İstanbul; James Robertson

79bec849-104d-5cdc-a478-1cfc829ea187.name: Les Ponts du Chemin de fer près de Doummar, Syrie (Doummar Railway Bridges, Syria)
79bec849-104d-5cdc-a478-1cfc829ea187.description: Dummar was one of the final stations on the Beirut–Damascus railway before the line reached Damascus-Baramkeh. It is situated approximately seven kilometres by rail from the terminus, after the stations of the Barada valley and immediately before Damascus. The postcard, captioned "Les Ponts du Chemin de fer près de Doummar", focuses on the railway infrastructure and shows the track curving across a bridge through the densely wooded landscape surrounding the Dummar region. In the early 1930s, a cement factory was established at Dummar, close to the railway and Dummar station. Its location allowed the industrial complex to make use of the railway infrastructure.

7bb89a63-82a6-5695-bd9f-cf857d8d19fb.name: *Northern side of the tomb of the Christian woman. Excavations carried out by detachment of the Zouave regiments, under the direction of Berbrugger* \[curator of the *Musée d'Alger*\].
7bb89a63-82a6-5695-bd9f-cf857d8d19fb.short_description: Adrien Berbrugger (1801–1869) was an archaeologist specialising in Algeria, who founded the first Musée d'Algérie in Algiers (1838). He visited the "tomb of the Christian woman" for the first time in 1835. This burial mound, located near Tipaza in the south of the Algerian Sahel, had misidentified as an erroneous French translation had rendered "Roman" as "Christian". Berburgger launched various archaeological campaigns which would demonstrate that it was in fact a royal mausoleum from Mauretania. in 1855, for the first time in the history of archaeological excavations, the work of archaeologists was photographed. This photograph is from a "pictorial report" created by Frère Moulin as he passed through Algiers, and shows Berbrugger (by the door), John Green (the archaeological campaign's photographer) and a dozen Zouaves who had taken part in the excavation.
keywords: Algeria; archaeological mission; roman antiquities

7becfe40-aaa5-590f-a2a3-17c23dfb1f52.short_description: Photograph of first year Faculty of Medicine students at Egyptian University. A decree was issued for the establishment of a public university under the name “The Egyptian University” in 1925, comprised of four faculties; literature, science, medicine and law. The Faculty of Medicine, annexed to Qasr al-`Ayni Hospital, is one of the leading hospitals in the Arab World.

7f1db941-399d-5b93-be52-3e4334ec577f.name: La Gare de Cadem, Damas (The Station of Cadem, Damascus)
7f1db941-399d-5b93-be52-3e4334ec577f.description: The Qadam Station in Damascus was part of the Hijaz Railway, located in Qadam district south of the city centre. The name Qadam (foot) derives from a local Islamic tradition associated with the Prophet Muhammad. The site was believed to mark the place where the Prophet dismounted from his camel during one of his journeys, leaving his footprint impressed on a stone. It was the main departure station for Mecca for several years, and until 1908, pilgrims to Mecca and Medina embarked at the station. They then transferred to the Hijaz Railway Station in central Damascus. The Qadam station remained important for transporting goods and was equipped with sidings, goods sheds, loading facilities and workshops serving the operations.

7f9082fe-da75-56c9-8c44-bba718558f12.name: Ottoman Clothing Album
7f9082fe-da75-56c9-8c44-bba718558f12.short_description: With the political developments of the 19th century, interest in the East increased steadily in the western world. Everything belonging to the East was the centre of interest for western observers. As a result, close to 160 artists visited Istanbul in the 19th century. Pascal Sébah (1823-86) was a pioneer photographer who worked in Istanbul. Sébah opened a photography studio known as "El Chark " in Pera in 1857. The studio's most successful period started with the Vienna Universal Exhibition in 1873. Sébah formed a partnership with Joaillier Polycarpe in 1885. In 1899, the two partners bought Abdullah Frères's archives. For the Vienna Universal Exhibition in 1873, Pascal Sébah prepared *The Ottoman Clothing Album* to be exhibited at the Ottoman Stand.

8138d27f-0df1-5e19-884f-c3f2fabf66df.name: Istanbul Main Post Office Opening Ceremony
8138d27f-0df1-5e19-884f-c3f2fabf66df.short_description: The Istanbul Main Post Office is an office building for postal services located at the *Sirkeci* quarter of the faith district in Istanbul, Turkey. It was designed by architect Vedat Tek in the First Turkish National architectural style and was constructed between 1903 and 1909. (Vedat Tek was a notable Turkish architect, who has been one of the leading figures of the First Turkish National Architectural Movement. He studied at the *École Centrale Paris*, graduating with a degree in civil engineering before he got his further education in architecture at the *Ecole des Beaux Arts* in Paris.) The four-story building houses a post office, the *Sirkeci* Post Office, office space for regional administration and also since 2000 the Istanbul Postal Museum. It is Turkey's largest post office building.

8139411f-fd90-565b-b236-4329f1f00269.name: Italian troops landing in Libya
8139411f-fd90-565b-b236-4329f1f00269.description:
In October 1911 the Italian government sent an expeditionary force of 34,000 men to Libya, with the goal of colonising the country. The conquest proved much more difficult than the Italian government had expected and it soon needed to send reinforcements; at the end of 1911, the Italian army in Libya had reached 103,000 men.  
Many Italians supported the colonial conquest of Libya, believing that the country would provide settlement opportunities for Italian migrants (in the first decade of the 20th century, Italian migrants abroad averaged 600,000 per year). Their hopes went mostly disappointed: in 1927, barely 26,000 Italians had settled in Libya. Only in the 1930s, after crushing Libyan anti-colonial resistance by means of ruthless repression, was the Italian government able to promote Italian settlement in Libya. By 1939, the Italian population in Libya reached almost 120,000.
8139411f-fd90-565b-b236-4329f1f00269.holder: Italian Institute for African and Oriental Studies

81a863b7-0e26-5e2a-b1ac-55b331836571.name: The Consuls’ Square [Alexandria, Egypt] after the Fire
81a863b7-0e26-5e2a-b1ac-55b331836571.short_description:
The author of this picture, Luigi Fiorillo, was an Italian photographer who migrated to Alexandria (Egypt) around 1870 and opened a successful photography shop. In 1877, he participated as photographer in an expedition to Shewa region (Ethiopia), organised by the Italian Geographical Society, and ten years later in an Italian military expedition for the colonial conquest of Eritrea.  
In 1882, Fiorillo was one of the few Europeans who remained in Alexandria after the anti-foreign rioting and documented the consequences of the British bombardment on Alexandria of July 11th. He collected 50 pictures of the city ruins in an album titled “Souvenir d'Alexandrie: Ruines, 1882”.  
On the back of some photos that he took in the 1880s, Fiorillo defines himself as “le photographe de Son Altesse le Prince Mohammed Toussoun Pasha” (the photographer of his Majesty Prince Mohammed Toussoun Pasha). Luigi Fiorillo died in 1898.
81a863b7-0e26-5e2a-b1ac-55b331836571.author: Giulia Barrera

826abea9-d0a5-5b38-9d39-fb3cd81ac626.name: The Şirket-i Hayriyye’s Excursion Steamship
826abea9-d0a5-5b38-9d39-fb3cd81ac626.short_description: The Şirket-i Hayriyye was the name of a steam boat joint-stock company which carried passengers and cargo on the Bosporus from 1854 to 1945. The company was established with the approval of the Sultan Abdulmecid. The steam boats belonging to company were sent from European countries, primarily Britain. The first captains of this boats were almost all of Rûm origin. After the establishment of the Republic of Turkey, the company and its goods were purchased by the state.

82ced29b-1974-5648-8a77-a399212ae4e2.name: The horses presented by the Sultan of Morocco to the King of Italy on the occasion of the official visit to Italy by a Moroccan delegation
82ced29b-1974-5648-8a77-a399212ae4e2.short_description:
In 1890, the Sultan of Morocco sent Hagi El Maati el Mazamizi as an Ambassador to Italy. The Ambassador landed in Naples on June 7th and arrived by train in Rome on June 13th. At the railway station, he was received by the Mayor or Rome, the Prefect, and other authorities. A military band was playing and military men in high uniform were paraded in the station to greet the Ambassador.  
Outside the station, three of the King’s gala carriages were waiting for the ambassador and a military unit was paraded in his honour. Some carabinieri in high uniform escorted the ambassador to the hotel.  
Hagi El Maati el Mazamizi presented the King with gifts, including some superb horses that the King immensely appreciated. The King presented the Ambassador with a magnificent small gold and diamond box, and a hunting rifle and gave gold watches to the members of his escort.
82ced29b-1974-5648-8a77-a399212ae4e2.holder: State Library of Modern and Contemporary History

837581e0-006f-52d2-82bf-795b4cf10463.name: Portrait of Abraham Behor And Nisim Camondo
837581e0-006f-52d2-82bf-795b4cf10463.short_description: Abraham Salomon's descendants, Abraham-Behor (1829-1889) and Nisim (1830-1889) were partners in banking. As a rival to the Ottoman Bank, The Camondo Family established the Ottoman Empire Company-i Umumiyesi (*Societe Generale de l'Empire Ottoman*) with a capital of two million pounds in 1864. Because of the establishment of the Credit General Ottoman Bank in 1868, the Camondo Brothers decided to move the bank to Paris with the idea that the Bank should have absolutely no external links. Abraham-Behor became president of the institution of the *Alliance Israelite Universelle* in 1864. This institution – which instructed students in French in the name of modernization and westernization – was founded to improve the material and spiritual conditions of the Jews and to ensure the spread of education in İstanbul.

840c6c73-9390-5b9c-ad84-481ed38f888d.name: Waterway in Nizwa, Oman
840c6c73-9390-5b9c-ad84-481ed38f888d.description: The *aflaj* (singular *falaj*) are one of the oldest irrigation systems still in use today. Its origins date back to 5,000 years ago, though the example here is from AD 500. Its channels convey water from underground sources, springs and stream flow to villages and towns all around Oman. This system is employed as a primary water source for agricultural and domestic purposes, accounting for more than 30% of water usage across Oman. Using gravity forces to maintain the flux of water and its distribution, it has emerged as a distinguished social, cultural and economic emblem of the Omani landscape. The responsibility for the maintenance of working falaj and the distribution of water to different settlements lies with these communities. Despite the existence of numerous wells that provide potable water, the presence of aflaj waterways is of pivotal significance to the agricultural prosperity of Oman. The Falaj Daris, seen here, are the largest of the aflaj in Oman, and played a big part in Nizwa’s former prosperity as the capital of Oman in the 6th and 7th centuries AD. In 2006, the Aflaj Irrigation System was inscribed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site and consequently granted governmental protection.
840c6c73-9390-5b9c-ad84-481ed38f888d.author: Yelyzaveta Basysta
keywords: Water; aflaj; irrigation systems.

845b837c-4ea7-514d-9566-c311425098ea.name: La Gare de Hedjaz, Damas (The Hijaz Station, Damascus)
845b837c-4ea7-514d-9566-c311425098ea.description: Standing before the Hijaz Railway Station is a small rectangular sabil (public fountain), one of the surviving elements of the station complex. Originally located in the centre of the spacious Hijaz Square, the sabil was later relocated to its present position on the pavement in front of the station. The fountain is designed with four faces, each fitted with a water spout, providing drinking water to the public. It represents a continuation of the Islamic tradition of providing free water within public spaces. A commemorative inscription was added later to honour Dr Muslim al Baroudi, who was killed during the French bombardment of Damascus in 1945 while carrying out his humanitarian duties, making the fountain a memorial integrated into the historic setting of the station.

84d0e24a-757f-5557-8920-19da45663b48.description: This album of 39 images documents the construction of the Hijaz Railway. It photographs two important stretches of the network: the route between Damascus and Maʿan, and the line connecting Daraʿa with Haifa. Its photographs record the remarkable engineering achievements required to negotiate difficult and varied terrain, while also illustrating the railway’s role in strengthening connections across the empire. Alongside tunnels, bridges and stations, the images capture the engineers, officials and labourers whose work made the project possible.

869766dc-71ca-53a7-b67f-e1ed2b58d4ac.name: La Goulette
869766dc-71ca-53a7-b67f-e1ed2b58d4ac.short_description: The expansion of the city of Tunis necessitated the construction of a large modern port which would be accessible to large-tonnage ships. Thus, in the early years of the French protectorate, the port of Tunis, La Goulette, saw a sharp increase in traffic. As well as a fishing port, the primary function of La Goulette, it also became an industrial centre thanks to the construction of a power plant on the north side of the canal, which served the tramways and the electric railway going to the northern suburbs. Finally, on the eve of the war, La Goulette had also become a residential town, particularly popular in summer for its seaside resorts.

87367afd-5729-556e-a43a-bec2611cfa83.name: *Napoléon II's journey to Algeria, 7 June 1865*
87367afd-5729-556e-a43a-bec2611cfa83.short_description: Napoléon III visited Algeria twice during his reign (in 1860 and 1865). It was unusual at this time for the French head of state to travel outside the country, so these visits attracted much attention. They also allowed Napoléon to show how important Algeria was to him. He wanted to judge the complex situation which had been described to him in various reports for himself. A lavish welcome was prepared for him wherever he went during both his visits. This image, for example, shows an arc de triomphe which was erected in his honour at the terminus of a small mining train at Bouhamza.
keywords: Diplomacy; Algeria; France; colonies; Napoléon III

8789877a-2d27-5791-8029-f3833b2e3bfb.name: German “Jildirim Postcard”.
8789877a-2d27-5791-8029-f3833b2e3bfb.description: This photograph depicts a group of restrained men gathered beside railway tank wagons on the Hijaz railway network during the First World War. Although their precise identity cannot be established from the image alone, the visible chains indicate that they were under military or administrative custody. During the war, the Hijaz Railway and its connecting lines transported not only troops and military supplies, but also labour detachments, conscripts and detainees, revealing the railway's role as an instrument of wartime administration and control. For many inhabitants of Bilad al-Sham, the years of Safarbarlik (from the Ottoman Turkish seferberlik, meaning military mobilisation) were remembered as years of uncertainty and loss. Many families were separated by military service, others by compulsory labour or detention, while entire communities endured famine, displacement and social disruption. In local collective memory, Safarbarlik's presence in folk songs and stories embodies the human cost of the First World War, transforming an official term of mobilisation into a symbol of collective suffering for the region.

"

87c48141-97a3-540d-a2e9-0fe778814f0f.name: Dérivation du Barrada près de Damas. (Division of the Barada River near Damascus)
87c48141-97a3-540d-a2e9-0fe778814f0f.description: A steam train travelling beside a diversion of the Barada River near Damascus, as identified by its French caption, Dérivation du Barrada près de Damas. The tracks and watercourse occupy the narrow corridor between the surrounding hills. The Barada River is divided into a network of branches before entering Damascus, historically supplying water to the city and the agricultural landscape of the Ghouta (the countryside region surrounding Damascus ). The railway belongs to the Beirut–Damascus railway, constructed by the Société de Construction des Batignolles and completed in 1895.

8a6cfa46-5a45-55b6-8e98-9c89d191db94.name: Primary students at a village school in central Italy, which followed the teaching methods introduced by Maria Montessori
8a6cfa46-5a45-55b6-8e98-9c89d191db94.short_description:
When Italy became a nation state in 1861, the illiteracy rate in the country was 78 per cent. In 1901, it was still at 56 per cent. Illiteracy was particularly high in the countryside. In 1877, the “Coppino Law”, made elementary schools mandatory and free of charge.  
Maria Montessori (1870-1952) was a medical doctor who developed innovative teaching methods for primary-school children. Her educational methods were first applied in the first decade of the 20th century. They met with great success and were applied in thousands of schools all over Europe and North America.
8a6cfa46-5a45-55b6-8e98-9c89d191db94.author: Giulia Barrera

8aa9aed7-b2ea-50bd-90ad-08ec6d53d8f4.short_description: The engineer, painter and architect Prisse d'Avennes (1807–1879) lived in Egypt for 20 years, and was to a great extent assimilated into Egyptian society and had adopted many Egyptian customs. Other figures, such as Delacroix in Morocco and Flaubert in Egypt, were also fascinated by the landscapes, knowledge and customs of these countries, which became the inspiration for many of their works, thus initiating the trend of "Orientalist writing".

Taken at a time when goods were being transported to the United Arab Republic (UAR), the political union of Egypt and Syria from 1958 to 1971, the image reflects both the logistics of mid-20th century air transport and the UAR’s pursuit of modernization and international connectivity.

8d0345df-1e22-5450-8f37-706dc5be7d91.short_description: This photo from Enrico H. Giglioli's collection was taken by the Florentine naturalist during his travels around the world in 1865 and 1868 while advancing diplomatic and commercial relations between the newborn Italian state and the other nations. The images seem to have been created spontaneously to show ethnocentric diversity. The ethnographic photographs in the Giglioli's collection are part of the historical archive of the Pigorini Museum. The origins of scientific activity and conservation of Museo Nazionale Preistorico Etnografico "Luigi Pigorini" in Rome can be traced back to the foundation in 1875 of the "Royal National Museum of Prehistory and Ethnography in Rome" within the buildings of the Roman College.

8d442666-d342-5c4d-9c43-c2e224624413.name: Photographic view entitled ‘*Prayers around the Ka‘ba*’
8d442666-d342-5c4d-9c43-c2e224624413.short_description: The photograph, which is entitled ‘*Prayers around the Ka‘ba*’, is signed by the Meccan doctor ‘Abd al-Ghaffar, the first resident of Mecca to photograph the Masjid al-Haram. In 1885 Christiaan Snouck Hurgronje, the first European photographer of Mecca, taught ‘Abd al-Ghaffar how to best use a camera and, when Snouck was expelled from the Hijaz, he left his photographic equipment with ‘Abd al-Ghaffar who went on to take a series of important photographs of the rituals of Hajj. Many of his photographs of Hajj were used in Snouck’s *‘Bilder aus Mekka’* published in 1889. (See: ARC.pt 784 Hajj and the Arts of Pilgrimage (Khalili Collections)).

8e570147-8f0e-58aa-a560-22e1e130385b.name: Le Boulevard El-Nassr, Damas (El-Nassr Boulevard, Damascus)
8e570147-8f0e-58aa-a560-22e1e130385b.description: Al Nasr Street in Damascus, previously known as Jamal Pasha Street, was renamed Al Nasr (Arabic: "Victory") in 1919. The street extends between the commercial centre near Suq al-Hamidiyya and the Hijaz Railway Station. Although an earlier route existed on the site, it was widened and monumentalized during the First World War under Jamal Pasha, the Military Governor of Ottoman Syria. The project formed part of a broader programme of urban transformation in the Ottoman provinces. The printed caption reads “Damas. — Le Boulevard El-Nassr un jour de fête,” ("Damascus—A Day of Celebration on El-Nassr Boulevard") and names the Damascus publishers Soubhi S. et Munir Aita. During this celebration, the street functioned as a gathering place on a scale that would have been difficult to accommodate within the narrow streets of Damascus's historic urban fabric. Soubhi and Munir Aita were photographers and imprint publishers active in Damascus, particularly during the 1920s.

8f55adc5-662c-55f8-a485-b18851210a66.name: Anatolian Railways
8f55adc5-662c-55f8-a485-b18851210a66.short_description: During the 19th century, new technologies radically transformed both travel and communications. The first railway in Anatolia was constructed between Izmir and Aydin. Ottoman railways were mainly built during the period of Abdülhamid II. The first railway in the Republic of Turkey was part of the İzmir-Aydın line, founded by a British company in 1860. The İzmir-Kasaba line was built in 1865, the Rumeli line in 1869-77, the Anatolia-Baghdad line in 1872 and the Mudanya-Bursa line in 1892.

8f60990a-2e19-50e5-b91c-31a7c8a103fd.name: Beirut Port before expansion
8f60990a-2e19-50e5-b91c-31a7c8a103fd.short_description: This photograph shows the Beirut port before its expansion. The dam was built under the command of Ibrahim Pasha. This old port underwent several important changes in the late 19th century, including the construction of a commercial tribunal and expansion of the port. This expansion involved the enlargement of existing buildings and filling areas of sea with rock brought in along the Nahr al-Kalb railway.

8f933cf6-939e-5018-be2c-726c4f9ca78a.name: Little Sicily
8f933cf6-939e-5018-be2c-726c4f9ca78a.short_description: Pictured here is an area, near the port of Tunis, where many immigrants from southern Italy had settled. Between 1865 and 1900, hundreds of small one or two-bedroom houses were built in the lower part of the Avenue Jules Ferry (today Avenue Habib-Bouguiba). The layout of the port allowed for the a rapid increase in the number of residents; a great many (mostly Sicilian) workers settled around the warehouses and workshops. Little Sicily therefore became both the home of the European working classes and the centre of the city's industrial activity. As Gaston Loth described it in 1905, "It's still Sicily, the children live in the streets, speak Arabic but also French, it's a like a swarm of lewd, barely dressed sparrows."
8f933cf6-939e-5018-be2c-726c4f9ca78a.holder: Institut Supérieur d’Histoire Contemporaine de la Tunisie

905cb8f2-54fa-520a-b0bc-209a26809787.short_description: With the political developments of 19th century, interest in the East increased steadily in the western world. Everything belonging to the East was the centre of interest for western observers. As a result, close to 160 artists visited Istanbul in 19th century. Vassilaki Kargopoulo was of Greek descent. His first studio was opened in 1850 near the Russian Consulate. Between the years of 1859 and 1860, he began to attract the attention of customers from all sections of society. He focused on Ottoman clothing and street vendors in 1860.

9061ae44-6d42-5964-b1e3-97aaad10a6fc.short_description: The "Arènes de Lutèce" (a Gallo-Roman amphitheatre) was rediscovered during various urbanisation projects between 1869 and 1885. 90898679-94a2-5a74-9442-dce1eaec5acf.name: *Shepherd with his sheep*
90898679-94a2-5a74-9442-dce1eaec5acf.short_description: Sheep husbandry has always been a traditional agricultural occupation in the Romanian lands. Shepherds spent summers in mountainous regions, where they found pastures for their flocks, and descended into lower valleys for the winter. Transhumance is still practiced in Romania. During the Ottoman sovereignty, one of Moldavia and Wallachia's economical obligations towards the Porte was to send sheep, but also sheep wool, cheese, meat and tallow in the Ottoman Empire.

90b30aa0-1bcb-5a10-80c9-1a254c7529d3.name: A retrospective: Preparations for the exhibition of 1889 - the Eiffel Tower under construction
90b30aa0-1bcb-5a10-80c9-1a254c7529d3.short_description: For the Exposition Universelle (world fair) of 1889, France wanted to both celebrate the centenary of the 1789 revolution and also showcase its skill and inventiveness. The Eiffel Tower, a daring move in the world of cast-iron architecture, became first the symbol of the exhibition then of the city as a whole.

922ac1b0-e425-5db9-98ed-2ceda9b73f82.name: Zaytuna University
922ac1b0-e425-5db9-98ed-2ceda9b73f82.short_description: This photograph shows young students coming out of a class in the Zaytuna University. In fact, the mosque was not only a place of worship, but also a sizeable university. A number of theologians, litterateurs, and art and science scholars from all over the Arab world (with an emphasis on North Africa) founded, across various generations, the Zaytuna university in Tunis. The teaching was constantly being modernized and restructured during the 19th century, and particularly under the reign of Ahmed Pacha Bey and the viziership of the reforming minister Khaireddine (Khayr al-Din).

92891afc-502b-5609-8db7-99bf7bb50e6c.name: Franz Joseph I, Emperor of Austria (1830–1916)
92891afc-502b-5609-8db7-99bf7bb50e6c.short_description: Portrait of Emperor Franz Joseph as an officer of the *Kaiserjäger* (Elite regiment). He ruled Austria for 68 years. During his long reign he had cordial relation to the Sultans of the Ottoman Empire and visited Istanbul and Jerusalem. He died in 1916 during World War I.

928c9e9b-828a-5e50-84b7-70a3d3ef8c88.name: On the Royal Ship Marsala
928c9e9b-828a-5e50-84b7-70a3d3ef8c88.short_description: El Sayyid (or Sidi) Muhammad Idris al-Mahdi al Senussi (1889-1983), the grandson of the founder of the Senussi Sufi order, became head of the Senussi order in 1916. He took the title of Emir and ruled as King of Libya from 1951 through 1969. In 1920 Italy reached an agreement with him and invited him to Rome, where he met King Victor Emmanuel III. Idris’ relations with the Italian government later deteriorated, and he went into exile in Egypt and encouraged anti-Italian guerrilla from there.
928c9e9b-828a-5e50-84b7-70a3d3ef8c88.holder: Italian Institute for African and Oriental Studies

92edd2fe-ef09-5e83-baba-8f729535104a.name: Dolmabahçe Mosque and Square
92edd2fe-ef09-5e83-baba-8f729535104a.short_description: Dolmabahçe Mosque’s original construction was initiated by Bezm-i Alem Valide Sultan, the mother of Sultan Abdülmecid (1823-61). Upon her death, its construction was continued by her son. It is located in the southern part of the Dolmabahce Palace, situated on the coast. The mosque was opened for prayer services on 23 March 1855. Its architect is Garabet Balyan, a member of the Balyan family, who built various structures for the Ottoman Empire. The Dolmabahçe Mosque is adorned with various items of both Baroque and Ampir styles, which are reflected in the architectural design of that period. Also, an emergent architectural modernity in the mosque is its circular window design. Such a design had rarely been seen in mosques and civil architecture before this time.

92f613dc-01ad-5171-a5dd-b251dab90f70.name: Photograph of Krste Petkov Misirkov with his friends
92f613dc-01ad-5171-a5dd-b251dab90f70.short_description: Krste Petkov Misirkov (1874–1926) is the author of the book “On Macedonian Matters”, which was published in Sofia in 1903. This work is a starting point in explaining Macedonian distinctiveness, having served as an intellectual and contemplative engine for generations of Macedonians fighting in the battlefield and in literature alike.

94bc8ed7-7428-5a36-9919-9335c90547df.name: Migration preparations of Muslim families to Turkey
94bc8ed7-7428-5a36-9919-9335c90547df.short_description: The 1923 population exchange between Greece and Turkey was based upon religious identity, and involved the Greek Orthodox citizens of Turkey and the Muslim citizens of Greece. The "Convention Concerning the Exchange of Greek and Turkish Populations" was signed at Lausanne, Switzerland, on 30 January 1923, by the governments of Greece and Turkey. During the migration waves during the 1896-97 riots in Crete, 40,000 Cretan Muslims had to migrate to territories under Ottoman rule: Lebanon, Syria and Anatolia. This photograph pertains to migration preparations from Lemnos to Turkey in 1924.
94bc8ed7-7428-5a36-9919-9335c90547df.holder: Population Exchange Museum (The Foundation of Lausanne Treaty Emigrants)

94c32a7d-017c-575e-a5ab-92b46e2819f5.name: A self-produced photocard showing a group of children and adults with travel snacks, waiting for a train
94c32a7d-017c-575e-a5ab-92b46e2819f5.description: A self-produced photocard showing a group of adults and children with provisions waiting for a train. Several heavily loaded camels stand behind the group, while baskets, bottles and other containers are carried by the people. A woman at the right holds a shallow basket containing what appears to be food. These provisions formed an important part of long-distance travel in the region. Before the railway, especially at Haj, caravans were used to transport travellers, merchandise and supplies southward, and merchants had their own camels to carry their loads toward Medina. After the railway, the use of animal transport remained important to move cargo and passengers to specific locations far from the stations.
94c32a7d-017c-575e-a5ab-92b46e2819f5.bibliography: Ochsenwald, William, “Hijaz Railway”, in *Oxford Bibliographies in Islamic Studies*, Oxford University Press. Published April 24, 2012; updated July 5, 2018.
keywords: Travel; Train; Pilgrimage; Hajj; Transportation; Merchants

9533b9d1-3fe7-5fb5-bdef-8dce66c03f06.name: The Black Obelisk of Assyrian King Shalmaneser III
9533b9d1-3fe7-5fb5-bdef-8dce66c03f06.short_description: The Black Obelisk of Assyrian King Shalmaneser III was excavated by a British expedition at Nimrud (Iraq) in 1846. There was great excitement when it was found to contain reference to Biblical king Jehu. Furthermore, it depicted his image, still the oldest image of a king of Israel.

9534f19d-962c-5eca-86f4-b14cd7c8f7af.name: Deutsches Soldaten u. Eisenbahnerheim in Eski-Chehir. Das Heim wurde 1916 eröffnet. (The Home of German Soldiers and Railway workers. The home was opened in 1916.
9534f19d-962c-5eca-86f4-b14cd7c8f7af.description: The Home of German Soldiers and Railwaymen (Deutsches Soldaten und Eisenbahnerheim) in Eskişehir opened in 1916. This institution served German military personnel and railway employees during the First World War. The building reflects the sizeable German railway community that had developed around Eskişehir after the town became an important junction of the German-backed Anatolian railway network. The Ottoman Anatolian Railway Company had already established a German Railway School beside Eskişehir station, operating since 1898 for the children of European railway officials and workers.

954b0597-1e92-5222-bbca-efdc2174af21.short_description: An old photograph of the Egyptian Stock Market in Alexandria, one of the oldest stock markets in the world. Being a wealthy man, he was very well travelled. His photographs, which  remained anonymous for a long time but were among the first photographs to be taken in the Middle East.

97051bf0-5841-5c21-bc4b-4e7e702b5270.name: Museo Nazionale Preistorico Etnografico 'L. Pigorini' (National Museum of Prehistory and Ethnography), Exhibition Room
97051bf0-5841-5c21-bc4b-4e7e702b5270.short_description: The origins, in terms of scientific activity and conservation, of the Museo Nazionale Preistorico Etnografico "Luigi Pigorini" in Rome, can be traced back to the foundation in 1875 of the “Regio Museo Nazionale Preistorico Etnografico di Roma" (Royal National Museum of Prehistory and Ethnography). Initially the museum was located in a wing of the Palazzo del Collegio Romano built in the late 16th century by the Society of Jesus. This rare image represents the old arrangement of one of the rooms of the Roman College, where the collection of antiquities and curiosities gathered by Father Athanasius Kircher was kept after the foundation of the museum. According to the intentions of its founder, Luigi Pigorini, the purpose of this new institution was not only to gather together the remains of Italian prehistoric culture and the "primitive" cultures of other European and non-European peoples in a "central" museum located in the new capital of the Kingdom, but above all to support, promote and participate in research by palethnologists in Italy.
97051bf0-5841-5c21-bc4b-4e7e702b5270.holder: National Museum of Prehistory and Ethnography “Luigi Pigorini”

9825c289-5dc5-5c51-b115-fa920eda0b57.name: The artificial channel built at Shellal, during the construction of the first dam on the Nile
9825c289-5dc5-5c51-b115-fa920eda0b57.short_description: In the year 1900, Count Giulio d’Aspremont, an Italian diplomat, visited the construction site of the first dam across the Nile (today known as the Aswan Low Dam or Old Aswan Dam). He took several photographs of the works and of the monuments on the island of Philae that were slated to be submerged by the water. He published some of them on the *Bulletin of the Italian Geographical Society*, where he wrote that up to 2,000 Italian workers were employed in the works (as stone-cutters, miners and masons), out of a total labour force of about 10,000 or 12,000; an Italian village had sprung up on the Nile banks, with modest little houses, trattorias and shops.
9825c289-5dc5-5c51-b115-fa920eda0b57.author: Patrizia Pampana

98465502-2fc0-537f-8943-a5b60d87d5c5.name: Osman Hamdi Bey (Getting mold of Antiochus relief During the excavation of Mount Nemrut)
98465502-2fc0-537f-8943-a5b60d87d5c5.short_description: In the 19th century, efforts were in place to modernize the Ottoman Empire, as many of the leading statesmen were exposed to Western ideas through education and travel. The museum was founded by decree in 1891 as the Imperial Museum. The first curator and founder of the museum was Osman Hamdi. Hamdi began construction of the main building in 1881, and it achieved its present neo-Greek form in 1908. The architect was Alexander Vallaury. It is one of the prominent structures built in the neoclassical style in Istanbul. Osman Hamdi, during his tenure as museum director, launched the first Turkish scientific excavations. He carried out archaeological excavations at Mount Nemrut, Laguna and Sidon.
keywords: Painting; Osman Hamdi Bey; orientalist Turkish painters; archaeological excavations

9863f692-894f-5cb2-b496-b0ec25aba740.name: Kabyle mother with her child
9863f692-894f-5cb2-b496-b0ec25aba740.short_description: Western photographers were particularly interested in both women's daily lives, and family life. This photo from 1920 shows a Kabyle woman carrying her baby with a look of pride on her face.

9a4c0c9b-0185-5c3b-94c2-863439ee8c9a.short_description: In the 19th century, efforts were in place to modernize the Ottoman Empire, as many of the leading statesmen had been exposed to Westernizing ideas through education and travel. Construction of the main building began in 1881, attaining its present neo-Greek form in 1908. The architect was Alexander Vallaury. The site of the museum belonged to the Topkapı Palace outer gardens. It is a prominent structure built in the neoclassical style in Istanbul.

9a890b71-5d5a-57ef-b26d-c4592e54b5ac.name: Beirut Tramway station
9a890b71-5d5a-57ef-b26d-c4592e54b5ac.short_description: This photograph shows the main tramway station in Beirut, located on Corniche el Nahr Street by the river in the district of Burj Hammud. It was constructed in 1906 under the command of the Ottoman government, and housed the carts and the engineering station.
9a890b71-5d5a-57ef-b26d-c4592e54b5ac.author: Jeff El-Msanne, Rita El Hachem

9aa7bece-df44-557d-99af-6cb4118c4095.name: The yacht Makook III built by the Fratelli Orlando Company (Livorno, Italy) for the Egyptian Khedive Abbas Hilmi
9aa7bece-df44-557d-99af-6cb4118c4095.short_description: In 1910, the Khédivé of Egypt contracted the construction of a yacht to the shipyards Cantieri Gallinari of Livorno, Italy. This company went bankrupt and its business was absorbed by the Fratelli Orlando shipyards, from Livorno as well. After improving the project, the Fratelli Orlando started building the yacht in 1913 and delivered it to the Khédivé Hilmì Abbas in May 1914.  In recognition of the high quality of work on the yacht engineer Giuseppe Orlando was granted the Ottoman decoration of the Order of Osmanieh.
9aa7bece-df44-557d-99af-6cb4118c4095.author: Daniela Tazzi

9b3b7415-4847-52e1-a035-b476f65ee03e.name: Viaduct on the Haifa–Dar‘a line
9b3b7415-4847-52e1-a035-b476f65ee03e.description: This postcard depicts a viaduct on the Haifa–Dar'a section of the Hijaz Railway, identified on the image as the "Chemin de fer Hamidié du Hidjaz (Caifa–Deraa)". Published by the Société Lumière of Lyon, it presents the railway’s substantial engineering works within the landscape of Palestine. The postcard was circulated through the Levant, bearing French Levant postage stamps postmarked Beirut, Syria, on 11 October 1905 and Smyrna, Ottoman Turkey, on 17 October 1905.
9b3b7415-4847-52e1-a035-b476f65ee03e.holder: The Nasser D. Khalili Collection of Hajj and The Arts of Pilgrimage

9b43f3ea-5b0a-57f2-be8e-3ff0d20fe6f6.name: Beirut Port during its expansion
9b43f3ea-5b0a-57f2-be8e-3ff0d20fe6f6.short_description: This photograph shows the Beirut port during its expansion, which involved filling areas of sea with rock were brought along the Nahr al-Kalb railway.
9b43f3ea-5b0a-57f2-be8e-3ff0d20fe6f6.author: Jeff El-Msanne, Julien El Khoury

9b7af802-1ae8-51cf-9420-82e3e2b1c459.name: Photograph showing Khan Antun Bey Square
9b7af802-1ae8-51cf-9420-82e3e2b1c459.short_description: Pictured here is the Khan at Khan Antoun Bey square. The building housed trading offices on the ground and first floors and foreign consulates on the upper floors. There was also an inner courtyard used for parking the consuls' horse-drawn carriages. It was built in 1853 by Antoun Bey Najjar, a merchant who made his fortune in Constantinople. Located by the port, the construction of this building is a reflection of the increasing importance of trade between Beirut and the West following the redevelopment of the port area in 1841. The khan was an important centre for business and trade, and later served many different functions, housing foreign consulates, Ottoman administrative offices, the postal service, merchants' offices and Beirut's first bank.
9b7af802-1ae8-51cf-9420-82e3e2b1c459.author: Hady El Hajj, Jennifer Harb, Cynthia Karaki
keywords: Khan; Souk; Trade; Economy; Beirut

9c17568a-e2ca-5524-b5ae-c2d13aa4c2ac.name: The Beirut water factory
9c17568a-e2ca-5524-b5ae-c2d13aa4c2ac.short_description: Located in the suburb of Dbayeh, this factory provided the daily water supply for all of Beirut. The company was founded in 1873 and the factory was first opened in 1896. The water was taken from the Nahr al-Kalb river and distributed across a large water network.
9c17568a-e2ca-5524-b5ae-c2d13aa4c2ac.author: Jeff El-Msanne, Rita El Hachem
keywords: Water; Economy

9c39a32f-844c-5e79-9249-d24aa6612ad5.name: Siamese diplomatic service
9c39a32f-844c-5e79-9249-d24aa6612ad5.short_description: in 1861, Mongkut, the King of Siam, sent a diplomatic service to Paris, not in order to create an alliance, but to preserve their independence by sending messages of good will to various European sovereigns. Napoléon III organised a lavish reception at the Palais Fontainebleau, recalling the Siamese reception which Louis XIV received in 1684. This photo reveals the importance of the Siamese delegation (three ambassadors and ten attachés in their military dress) accompanied by the Abbot Larnaudie, interpreter for the Siamese court.
keywords: Diplomacy; colonies; Siam; France

9cd33c79-f888-5848-ab0a-471109e32fbf.name: German military (propaganda) postcard (Feldpostkarte) published by F. Volckmar, Leipzig
9cd33c79-f888-5848-ab0a-471109e32fbf.description: Published in Leipzig by F. Volckmar as part of the German series Die Türkei im Weltkriege (Turkey in the World War), this field-postcard presents Jamal Pasha walking beside a train at a Damascus station with the figure described in its caption as the “Sharif of Mecca.” Ali Haydar Pasha, recognised as Sharif after Husayn ibn Ali by the Ottoman government, launched the Arab Revolt in 1916. Ali Haydar did not gain effective control of Mecca, making the title a political claim rather than an uncontested reality. Jamal Pasha, commander of the Ottoman Fourth Army and governor-general of the Syrian provinces during the war, was remembered locally as Jamal Pasha al Saffah “the blood-shedder” or “the butcher.” The name was associated particularly with his repression of Arab political activists and his order to execute prominent intellectuals, journalists and former officials after controversial wartime trials in Beirut and Damascus. The postcard was produced for a German audience, promoted an image of continued local loyalty to the Ottoman state and a unity within the German–Ottoman alliance, while concealing the conflict over control of the region and Hijaz.
9cd33c79-f888-5848-ab0a-471109e32fbf.bibliography:
Fawaz, Leila Tarazi, *A Land of Aching Hearts: The Middle East in the Great War*, Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Press, 2014.  
  
Akgül, Önder Eren, “War on the Desert: The Militarization of the Sinai and Its Greater Syrian Sacrificial Frontier during World War I.” in *International Journal of Middle East Studies*, 56:1 (2024).
keywords: Photography; military; Propaganda; War; World War

9cfc95e2-dcd3-56fd-b37e-253ac1e09a34.name: *Immigrants* \[on Ellis Island\]. *Two Italian kids*
9cfc95e2-dcd3-56fd-b37e-253ac1e09a34.short_description: At the start of the 20th century millions of Italian families emigrated to America by boat, driven by economic misery and the hope of a better life. Once they arrived, the immigrants were taken to have a number of checks done by the Ellis Island authorities, as they had to satisfy certain standards (hygiene, health) or risk being repatriated. One can understand, therefore, why these two well-dressed Italian children seem anxious.
keywords: Italy; immigration

9d2ab4b5-fef1-530e-806a-e497c463b2a5.name: An old exhibition from Tiled Kiosk
9d2ab4b5-fef1-530e-806a-e497c463b2a5.short_description: The Tiled Kiosk is a pavilion set within the outer walls of Topkapı Palace that dates from 1472. It was built by the Ottoman sultan Mehmed II as a pleasure palace or kiosk. The building was used as the Imperial Museum between 1875 and 1891. In 1953, it was opened to the public as a museum of Turkish and Islamic art, and was later incorporated into the Istanbul Archaeology Museums. The collections of the Tiled Kiosk Museum consist of about 2000 artefacts belonging to the Seljuk and Ottoman eras, dating from the 11th-20th centuries. These artefacts include those that existed when the museum was incorporated into the İstanbul Archaeological Museums due to its proximity as well as those acquired through excavations, purchases, donations and confiscations.
9d2ab4b5-fef1-530e-806a-e497c463b2a5.dates: The Tiled Kiosk: 15th century; The photograph: 19th century
keywords: Istanbul Archaeological Museum; Tiled Kiosk

9d99f2a0-088c-5411-b1e4-aab5af09edf0.name: Photograph showing maintenance of the telephone network in Tangier
9d99f2a0-088c-5411-b1e4-aab5af09edf0.description: A photograph taken by a German photographer in 1923 showing maintenance of the telephone network that had been installed in Tangier since 1883.
keywords: Telephone; technical innovations; communication; telephone network; photograph; visual document; changes in urban space; modernisation; modern city; city

9d9c9b21-26f5-5feb-9433-34771e40c124.name: Nikola Karev
9d9c9b21-26f5-5feb-9433-34771e40c124.short_description: Nikola Karev (1877–1905) was one of the ideological leaders and organizers of the Uprising of Ilinden. The uprising broke out on the night of 2 August 1903. After taking over, Krushevo revolutionaries declared the Krushevo Republic on 3 August. The Headquarters of the uprising took the military control over the town. The other governing bodies were the Revolutionary Council, consisting of sixty of the most prominent citizens representing all nationalities, and the Government, consisting of six members. Vangel Dinu was the Prime Minister and Nikola Karev was the President of the Republic. Owing to the progressive socialist ideas of Nikola Karev and other revolutionaries, the Krushevo Republic was laid on truly democratic foundations and republican principles. Karev announced the Krushevo Manifesto as a truly democratic document addressing all nationalities living in Macedonia, regardless of their religion, envisioning equal rights for everyone.
9d9c9b21-26f5-5feb-9433-34771e40c124.author: Nada Andonovska (author), Dragan Georgiev, historian (consultant)
keywords: Revolutionary Council; Government

9dbfd8cd-e3bf-5f5f-bd09-c7f5a2634953.name: The Students’ Benevolent Fund of the Società Dante Alighieri
9dbfd8cd-e3bf-5f5f-bd09-c7f5a2634953.short_description: The Dante Alighieri Society – created in Italy in 1889 and still in existence ‒ is aimed at promoting Italian language and culture abroad; its Tunisian branch was established in 1893. In Tunisia the Dante Alighieri Society devoted its energies into promoting schooling and supporting school attendance. One should consider, in this regard, that the Italian community at the time was composed of workers, miners, and labourers and included several destitute members. The students’ benevolent fund of the Società Dante Alighieri (Patronato scolastico) was created in 1898 and was aimed at supporting school attendance of destitute children, by providing free books and clothes.
9dbfd8cd-e3bf-5f5f-bd09-c7f5a2634953.author: Giulia Barrera

9e555530-36a5-59e9-a179-0f1bdff61fd4.name: Seated *Pifferari*
9e555530-36a5-59e9-a179-0f1bdff61fd4.short_description: The first significant waves of Italian migration abroad began in the mid-19th century during a period of great economic difficulty, with most migrants travelling to neighbouring European countries. One example of this was the "pifferari" - Italian shepherds from Abruzzo or Calabria who sung traditional songs accompanied by pipes - who started arriving in Paris. The famous French artist Charles Nègre (1820–1880) often focussed his work on street scenes such as this one.

9e8a7ea8-8f60-59b4-af77-1fef1a414d6a.name: Construction of the Aswan Dam
9e8a7ea8-8f60-59b4-af77-1fef1a414d6a.short_description:
Photograph showing labourers during the construction of the Aswan Dam gates.  
Located in Upper Egypt, the Aswan Dam was the first water storage project in modern times.

9e9366e9-b19e-5ebc-a0ca-190882e7bb74.name: Deir el-Medina, Tomb of Kha at the moment of discovery
9e9366e9-b19e-5ebc-a0ca-190882e7bb74.short_description: Photo by an unknown author showing the archaeologists Ernesto Schiaparelli and Francesco Ballerini on the site of the tomb of the architect Kha, together with workers and the supervisor of the Italian Archaeological Mission to Egypt. The tomb of the architect Kha (TT 8) was discovered untouched in 1906 by Ernesto Schiaparelli inside the necropolis of Deir el-Medina. It was located inside the village of the craftsmen who worked at the royal tombs in the Valley of the Kings. The holder had been "Head of the royal necropolis" and "Superintendent to the works of the royal necropolis" in the middle of the 18th dynasty, during the reigns of Amenhotep II (1428–1397 BC), Thutmose IV (1397–1388 BC) and Amenhotep III (1388–1351 BC). The Museum of Egyptian Antiquities preserves all these goods, with the exception of a lamp, which is in the Egyptian Museum of Cairo, while a copy is on display at the Egyptian Museum in Turin.

9e9f6fa6-b6c4-5566-9322-05ca25f72753.name: The Railway Bridge from Anatolia
9e9f6fa6-b6c4-5566-9322-05ca25f72753.short_description: During the 19th century, new technologies radically transformed both travel and communications. The first railway in Anatolia was constructed between Izmir and Aydin. Ottoman railways were mainly built during the period of Abdülhamid II. The first railway in the Republic of Turkey was part of the İzmir-Aydın line, founded by a British company in 1860. The İzmir-Kasaba line was built in 1865, the Rumeli line in 1869-77, the Anatolia-Baghdad line in 1872 and the Mudanya-Bursa line in 1892.

9edbfb79-9af7-5f97-a619-da304ecfa112.name: Set of photos illustrating Livestock Room, Donkey Room and Sheeps and Wool Room at Fu`ad Agricultural Museum
9edbfb79-9af7-5f97-a619-da304ecfa112.short_description: The Fu`ad Agriculture Museum was considered the first of its kind in the Middle East and the Arab World during the 1930s. It was inaugurated during the time of King Faruq, the son of King Fu`ad, and houses a large number of collections related to agricultural and rural environments, as well as agricultural plants and animals.
9edbfb79-9af7-5f97-a619-da304ecfa112.dates: 16 January 1938 (Photos taken during the inauguration of the museum)

9ee00ba7-2731-5d14-b9bf-0d46da259600.name: Ismail, Khedive of Egypt (1830–1895)
9ee00ba7-2731-5d14-b9bf-0d46da259600.short_description: Portrait of Ismail, Khedive of Egypt (1830–1895), who financed the construction of the Suez Canal. Because of the enormous costs of the building and his reform measures, Egypt's debt rose from three million pounds sterling to 100 million pounds sterling. In 1875 Egypt was bankrupt and Ismail Pasha was forced to sell 176,602 shares to Great Britain for 3,976,582 pounds sterling. Egypt came under financial control of France and Great Britain.
keywords: Ismail, Khedive of Egypt; Suez Channel; Great Britain

9f85fad2-9896-5d7d-84a8-ecc96ac39ee0.name: Picture  of Qasr al-Qatrane (here Catrané) on the Hijaz-Line with a basin for water-supply.
9f85fad2-9896-5d7d-84a8-ecc96ac39ee0.description: The large water basin at Qatraneh, identified in the French caption as Le grand Bassin à Catrané sur la ligne de Hydjaz. Behind it stands Qatraneh Fort, which was founded in 1531 under Sultan Süleyman I as part of a chain of fortified stopping places established to protect the pilgrimage caravan and secure water and supplies. Built of limestone and basalt, it has high crenellated walls, arrow slits and projecting machicolations, with rooms arranged around a narrow courtyard. Beside it lies the square reservoir, measuring about seventy metres on each side, used to collect seasonal runoff for travellers and animals. Once the Hijaz Railway followed the older pilgrimage corridor, Qatraneh became a railway station and the existing reservoir was reused as a water source. A 1906 report records that the shallow basin lost water through evaporation but remained valuable to railway construction and operation.

a16e766d-fa06-5cca-9cee-d7168a62177e.name: La Gare de Baramke, Damas (Baramkeh Station, Damascus)
a16e766d-fa06-5cca-9cee-d7168a62177e.description: Baramkeh Station, established in 1895 on the western side of Damascus, was a major passenger and freight station serving the Beirut–Damascus railway. A substantial railway complex, it contained warehouses for railway equipment, places for rent, two large yards with long platforms for loading and unloading goods, and a dedicated passenger area. It was an important gathering point for passengers travelling westward and to Beirut. Located in the Baramkeh district, in the northwestern part of a region previously known as Bustan al-Ahmar, the station was demolished during the urban redevelopment of Baramkeh in the late 1960s, and its site subsequently became an intercity bus terminal until 2007.

a18b6db1-d14e-59e8-adcd-89811928c6c2.name: Turkish embassy in Greece
a18b6db1-d14e-59e8-adcd-89811928c6c2.short_description: In the 18th century, the Ottoman empire started to open permanent embassies in various capitals of Europe in order to more closely follow developments there and carry out interstate diplomacy more regularly. During the 19th century, the Ottoman Empire entered into intense western influence in almost every field. With the opening of the Ministry of Foreign Affaris, Ottoman diplomacy attained an institutional structure.

a1f0d2c4-ed0e-520e-ae95-52264d8e107d.name: The patients in Darülaceze Hospital
a1f0d2c4-ed0e-520e-ae95-52264d8e107d.short_description: One of the world's largest photo archives, Abdülhamid II's photo archives – knows as the Yildiz Albums – contain about 37 thousand pictures from that period of the Ottoman Empire. The photo archives contain images of cities, buildings which were built by sultan, schools, students, soldiers, mosques, ports, government departments, shipyards, railways, bridges, bazaars, machines, locomotives and factories. Darülaceze Hospital was established in Okmeydanı, Istanbul İn 1895 on the instructions of Abdülhamid II for the care of elderly, homeless and disabled people in need.
a1f0d2c4-ed0e-520e-ae95-52264d8e107d.holder: Istanbul University, Nadir Eserler Kütüphanesi (Rare Books Library)

a318db34-bac0-5d0f-a3b5-606f258a4cf5.name: Ortaköy Mosque
a318db34-bac0-5d0f-a3b5-606f258a4cf5.short_description: The original Ortaköy Mosque was built in the 18th century. The current mosque, which was erected in its place, was ordered by the Ottoman Sultan Abdülmecid and built between 1854 and 1856. Its architects were father and son Garabet Amira Balyan and Nigoğayos Balyan (who also designed the nearby Dolmabahçe Palace and the Dolmabahçe Mosque), who designed it in the Neo-Baroque style. It was during the same century that the mosque rose to a higher level of importance on the European side of Istanbul. It is also known as “Great Mecidiye Mosque” and is one of the most beautiful samples of Baroque architecture in Istanbul.
keywords: Photograph; Old İstanbul Photograph; İstanbul

a3c1cda7-3cd5-5acd-9fe6-bbcc3a97be64.name: Photograph of Bab Idris street
a3c1cda7-3cd5-5acd-9fe6-bbcc3a97be64.description: Pictured here is Bab Idris street, leading to Bab Idris, the city's western gate and the entrance to the old town. By the time of Ahmad Bey al-Jazzar's reign (1777–1804), the city had four main gates: Bab al-Dirka to the south, Bab al-Santiya to the west, Bab al-Dabbagha to the north, and Bab al-Saraya to the east. Jazzar Pasha built fortifications between these four main gates, which was not a fortified gate. Other city gates included Bab Yaqub, also in the east, Bab Abu Nasr at Burj square, and Bab Idris. These non-military gates are reflections of the city's rapid expansion, particularly due to an increase in trade.
a3c1cda7-3cd5-5acd-9fe6-bbcc3a97be64.author: Hady El Hajj, Jennifer Harb, Cynthia Karaki
keywords: Gate; Military; Fortified; Portal; Expansion

a3cd6343-e399-52fc-beca-9b8315cf4639.name: *Panorama of the Compagnie Transatlantique* (French Line). *The "La Ville de Rome" steamer leaving the port of Algiers via Montenard*
a3cd6343-e399-52fc-beca-9b8315cf4639.short_description: The emergence of steam boats in the 19th century allowed important maritime trade relationships to develop. In 1855, the Pereire brothers adopted this new method of transport and founded the Compagnie Générale Transatlantique (The French Line). The first line built served New York. In the 1880s the company then established an important line from Marseille to North Africa, which consisted of a 12-steamer strong fleet, the "sister ships" of the "Ville de Rome", which was first put into use in 1881. In March 1889, the "Ville de Rome" was run aground and washed up on the shores of Menorca. The passengers were evacuated in time, but the storm caused the wreck of the ship to break in two.
a3cd6343-e399-52fc-beca-9b8315cf4639.artist: Photographer: Neurdein Frères; artist: Frédéric Montenard
keywords: Transports; boats; ports; Algeria

a43697f3-629f-54a0-ad35-dca00abfe608.name: Bau der Ḥiğâzbahn [graphic] : Schienenlegung bei Tebûk. 1906.
a43697f3-629f-54a0-ad35-dca00abfe608.alternate_name: Construction of the Hijaz railroad : Laying the rails near Tabuk. 1906 eng.
a43697f3-629f-54a0-ad35-dca00abfe608.description: This photograph entitled Bau der Ḥiğâzbahn [graphic] : Schienenlegung bei Tebûk. 1906 or Construction of the Hijaz railroad: Laying the rails near Tabuk. 1906 shows workers laying the rails near Tabuk as part of the Hijaz Railway. It is taken by Moritz Bernhard, and represents plate 56 in the portfolio: Bilder aus Palästina. Nord-Arabien und dem Sinai published in Berlin : Dietrich Riemer in 1916. It shows the harsh conditions these workers witnessed, working in a desert landscape under very difficult conditions. The image records the work of assembling the railway track as construction advanced southwards towards Medina, documenting the manual labour involved in extending the line through the desert.
a43697f3-629f-54a0-ad35-dca00abfe608.owner: Library of Congress Prints and Photographs Division
keywords: Photography; Print; Railroad; Railway; Saudi Arabia

a473894e-afa3-59b7-93f3-cec646d6e272.short_description: Photographs of the excavations carried out in Carthage in the 19th century by Delattre.

a47e2724-6e4b-5b5c-ad40-f8e2d5e40ecb.short_description: At the beginning of the 20th century, textile factories in Italy employed a high proportion of female workers.

a49b0d20-ff69-5123-aea8-1e3778e61417.name: Archaeological excavations
a49b0d20-ff69-5123-aea8-1e3778e61417.short_description: Photograph of a pyramid at Abusir. The photo documents the excavation carried out by Juncker, a member of the German archaeological mission. The photo shows the tents for the members of the mission during the excavation of some clay pottery. The photo is printed from glass plate negatives, and it was included in the special archive for the archaeological areas of Saqqara and Abusir.

a541b832-d774-57c4-adb6-f83fd670fffc.name: Museo Nazionale Preistorico Etnografico “L. Pigorini” (National Museum of Prehistory and Ethnography), Exhibition Room
a541b832-d774-57c4-adb6-f83fd670fffc.short_description: The origins, in terms of scientific activity and conservation, of the Museo Nazionale Preistorico Etnografico "Luigi Pigorini" in Rome, can be traced back to the foundation in 1875 of the “Regio Museo Nazionale Preistorico Etnografico di Roma" (Royal National Museum of Prehistory and Ethnography). Initially the museum was located in a wing of the Palazzo del Collegio Romano built in the late 16th century by the Society of Jesus. This rare image represents the old arrangement of one of the rooms of the Roman College, where the collection of antiquities and curiosities gathered together by Father Athanasius Kircher was kept after the foundation of the museum. According to the intentions of its founder, Luigi Pigorini, the purpose of this new institution was not only to gather together the remains of Italian prehistoric culture and the "primitive" cultures of other European and non-European peoples in a central museum located in the new capital of the Kingdom, but above all to support, promote and participate in research by palethnologists in Italy.

a59d3d62-bb02-5cce-b693-cc1d841ab3e1.name: Damaskus (Bahnhof Kadem). (Damascus, Qadem Station)
a59d3d62-bb02-5cce-b693-cc1d841ab3e1.description: The postcard records the wider landscape surrounding the Qadam Station, on the urban edge of Damascus. The spacious compound with scattered service buildings and temporary tents shows that railway stations could extend beyond their passenger facilities and logistical zones. The open terrain surrounding the station reflects Qadam's position on the southern outskirts of Damascus, where sufficient land existed for railway expansion before the line continued towards the south and the Holy Cities. The coexistence of the station with its trains and the animal transportation outside of it demonstrates that modern rail infrastructure remained closely integrated with traditional patterns of mobility and movement. As the main southern operational station, Qadam formed the transition between the densely inhabited city of Damascus and the long open journeys towards Hijaz.

a5f9ccce-bdce-5ea9-8c27-06ad29d2353c.name: *Construction of a dam at Noisiel. State of the works on the 5th of August 1885*
a5f9ccce-bdce-5ea9-8c27-06ad29d2353c.short_description: Although little-known today, Auguste Hippolyte Collard (1812–1880s) contributed significantly to the rise of photography in France. He chose to specialise professionally in the photography of important construction sites. Thanks to him, today we can reconstruct the building of, for example, the Marne Dam at Noisiel in 1885. This dam is associated with the famous chocolatier Menier who became a pioneer in the field of cocoa refining, introducing the use of water power, among other new methods for the refinement of cocoa.

a6877d51-e0ec-5242-8b80-88d89c3d2ab4.name: Gare Chemin de fer Bagdad, Alep (Aleppo-Baghdad Railway Station)
a6877d51-e0ec-5242-8b80-88d89c3d2ab4.description: The postcard depicts Aleppo's Baghdad Railway Station, with the French description: Alep – Gare Chemin de fer Bagdad (Aleppo-Baghdad Railway Station), completed in 1912 as the northern Syrian terminus of the Baghdad Railway branch linking the city with Muslimiyeh station and the main line toward Mesopotamia. Situated in what became known as the Baghdad Station district, north of Aleppo's historic centre, the station was part of the development of a new modern quarter organised around transport and commerce. The station was constructed of stone masonry with broad overhanging roofs supported by timber brackets, pointed-arched openings and a monumental entrance pavilion. It was connected to the Baghdad Railway by a branch rather than the principal trunk line. The station became a strategic commercial gateway linking Aleppo with Anatolia in the north, and Mesopotamia as part of the wider Ottoman railway network.

a7c102ce-f4bb-5330-8383-c17696408f62.name: Khayr al-Din Pacha
a7c102ce-f4bb-5330-8383-c17696408f62.short_description: Khayr al-Din Pacha brought in many reforms which significantly changed the precolonial period, to a great extent Westernizing the Beylik of Tunis, which was later portrayed as "modernization". This Mamluk of circasian origin was probably born in 1825, and came to Tunis as a child in 1840. He quickly climbed the ranks and took his father-in-law Mustapha Khaznadar's place as Chief Minister under the rule of Mohamed Sadok Bey from 1873 to 1877. He died in 1890 in Istanbul, where he had served as grand vizier. He appears tall and majestic in this photograph, and carries authority in his piercing gaze. His jacket is richly decorated, bearing the coat of arms of the sovereign who bought him and brought him to Tunis, Ahmed Bey (1835–1855).

a8683bd7-cbf6-5821-a911-6ea63acae710.name: The Khaldouniya
a8683bd7-cbf6-5821-a911-6ea63acae710.short_description: Founded in Tunis on 22 December 1896, this school can be best described as a sort of modern school. Today, it houses a bilingual library holding several thousand volumes and hundreds of manuscripts, attached to the Bibliothèque Nationale de Tunisie. Founded by the Young Tunisians (Harakat al-Shabab al-Tunisi) and directed by Béchir Sfar, the school's name is a direct reference to the great Arab thinker Ibn Khaldoun. It had the aim of disseminating scientific and practical knowledge in the Arab cultural sphere, particularly among the students of the Zaytuna Mosque, whose teachings were considered archaic and purely religious. The institution was built near the Zaytuna thanks to the support of the French Resident-General, René Millet, who drew up its regulations and in so doing notably failed to include political and religious discussions, choosing instead to focus on encouraging critical and reflective thinking.

a8ba1fa9-babe-58f8-a236-0758c7c190cc.name: A self-produced photocard showing a small typical Ottoman railway station
a8ba1fa9-babe-58f8-a236-0758c7c190cc.description: This postcard shows Beirut Railway Station on the Beirut–Damascus railway, Beirut. With around 140,000 inhabitants in the early 1860s, Beirut was the region's major port and commercial centre, while Damascus, with nearly 200,000 inhabitants, functioned as the provincial capital and an important market for many products. Before the railway, Beirut and Damascus were connected by a 108-km mule road not suitable for caravans; archives note that the journey took approximately four days. The railway concession was granted in 1891, and the 147 km Beirut–Damascus railway opened in 1895. An Ottoman timetable reproduced from the official Suriye Vilâyeti Salnâmesi (Annual of the Province of Syria) records two daily departures from Beirut, at 07:05 and 17:30, on a route comprising between twenty-five and thirty stops.

a9297ffd-8462-5dd7-8571-a2309301164e.name: Egypt. Mummies found in the kings' tomb in Thebes
a9297ffd-8462-5dd7-8571-a2309301164e.short_description: Félix Bonfils settled as a photographer in Libya in 1867. Helped by his assistants, he reproduced photographs taken during his travels in neighbouring countries. These pictures were sold in albums or individually, to tourists or painters exploring the Middle East. In this photograph a merchant of Thebes is pictured, napping amongst the mummies he sells. The mummies were then bought either by European collectors, or for other purposes (medical ingredients, etc.).

a946e99a-c0f3-5d45-9fb0-6eec1cfb9b75.name: The cutting of granite blocks for the construction of the first dam on the Nile. Many Italian stonecutters participated in the works
a946e99a-c0f3-5d45-9fb0-6eec1cfb9b75.short_description: In the year 1900, Count Giulio d’Aspremont (an Italian diplomat), visited the construction site of the first dam across the Nile (today known as the Aswan Low Dam or Old Aswan Dam). He took several photographs of the works and of the monuments on the island of Philae that were slate to be submerged by the water. He published some of them on the *Bulletin of the Italian Geographical Society*, where he wrote that up to 2,000 Italian workers were employed in the works (as stone-cutters, miners and masons), out of a total labour force of about 10,000 or 12,000; an Italian village had sprung up on the Nile banks, with modest little houses, trattorias and shops.

a94b6245-85b8-5f79-b98e-7c8a3c4249f7.name: Italian colonial soldiers (known as '*askari*') wounded in the battle of Maharuga (Tripolitania, Libya) receiving assistance
a94b6245-85b8-5f79-b98e-7c8a3c4249f7.short_description:
In this photo one can see African soldiers (presumably Eritrean) of the Italian colonial army. Italy used Eritrea foremost as a source of *askari* (soldiers) who were made to fight for Italy’s colonial conquests in Somalia, Libya and Ethiopia.  
Today, Eritrean migrants who traverse Libya report that they perceive a special hostility against them, because Libyans remember that Eritreans served in the Italian colonial army.

a95aa12b-08ad-5216-93c1-8009226cdb57.short_description: French agriculture in Tunisia began either through the establishment of large properties by private initiatives, or the introduction of settlers by the public authorities. This is a photograph from the "first phase" - one of the "companies" (of "French farms") had purchased a large plot of land, and employed a number of (largely Arab and Italian) workers to cultivate the land. It shows two combine harvesters which had been imported for the development of intensive cereal faming, and would have been used as advertising for Europeans considering investing in this type of agricultural "company".

a95b3b6a-66a7-5a79-99bd-6be598fec282.name: Dolmabahçe Palace Theatre under construction
a95b3b6a-66a7-5a79-99bd-6be598fec282.short_description: James Robertson came to Istanbul in 1841 to assist with modernization of the Imperial Mint and remained for 40 years, during which he served without interruption under no less than four Ottoman sultans. He started as head etcher in the Ottoman Mint. Then he began to take photos of Istanbul. He also painted watercolours, and in the early 1850s became interested in photography and went on to become a leading name among early photographers. Robertson’s Istanbul photographs are concerned primarily with the city’s historical monuments. They reveal the city’s magnificent Byzantine and Ottoman structures from different angles and with close-ups taken in an approach that is usually quite aesthetic. In this photo, Dolmabahçe Palace Theatre is seen under construction.
a95b3b6a-66a7-5a79-99bd-6be598fec282.author: Bahattin Öztuncay
keywords: Photography; İstanbul; History of architecture

aa4878d5-82c1-50ac-a798-91386bc0bd59.name: Maan Station, Hedjaz R.R. [i.e., Hejaz Railroad]
aa4878d5-82c1-50ac-a798-91386bc0bd59.description: This photograph of Maʿan station, preserved as a glass negative in the G. Eric and Edith Matson Photograph Collection at the Library of Congress, was produced by the American Colony Photo Department or its successor, the Matson Photo Service. One of 22000 photographs in the collection, it depicts a part of the railway beside a stone station building, with a pitched roof. The station served the Hijaz Railway in present-day Jordan, with the Damascus–Maʿan section opening in 1904. Long before the railway’s construction, Maʿan was an important stop on the Hajj caravan route and a frontier town between Syria and the Hijaz. Its pilgrimage fair contributed to its prosperity during the nineteenth century, as reflected in the accounts of Georg August Wallin, who visited in 1845 and 1848. During the Arab Revolt, the station and its surrounding defences became a focus of fighting, as recorded by T. E. Lawrence.

aaabc192-01bc-59ee-bc6c-ebd3ae07bab2.name: Station de Hijaz, Damas (The Hijaz Station, Damascus)
aaabc192-01bc-59ee-bc6c-ebd3ae07bab2.description: The Hijaz Railway Station is located on the western side of the Old City of Damascus, west of Bab al Nasr, near the entrance to Souq al Hamidiyah. It is situated at the intersection of al Nasr Street, Saadallah al Jabiri leading to al Halbouni area, and Muslim al Baroudi Street, which leads towards the Baramkeh district. The site where the station was built had previously served as the gathering place for pilgrims arriving from across Asia. Pilgrims assembled in Damascus before departing in a ceremonial caravan led by the Ottoman Governor of Damascus. The procession followed a route through the Midan district toward Qadam and continuing south toward the Hijaz.

aabb4c5f-7b18-5d94-a2c9-d82eb2eb1616.name: “Sartian Dervishes“ [Turkestan Qalandars]
aabb4c5f-7b18-5d94-a2c9-d82eb2eb1616.short_description: A photograph from the late 19th century depicts a group of wandering dervishes who reject the world, and whose external appearance suggests that they are not concerned with social conventions. A number of these mystics carry a begging bowl – they live from begging. Revealingly, the Sufis are known in Europe by the name of fakir and dervish, Arabic and Persian for "poor." Poverty and lack of possessions are the core features of their way of life. They are pious ascetics who scorn everything temporal and reject existing conventions, rules, and dogmata. The goal of these individuals is to experience God as the final reality. Following this programme, these "friends of God" have already contributed to the dissemination of Islam since the Middle Ages. Wherever they go, they preach – beyond all theological sophistry – their interpretation of an open-minded, and humane Islam. Not infrequently they pay for this with their lives – even today.

acc57934-ae32-5e43-8f31-305447337577.short_description: During the 19th century, new technologies radically transformed both travel and communications. Cendere Hamidian Water Pump Station was built by Abdülhamid II in 1902 at an altitude of 34 metres above sea level. With its function, architectural design and mechanical equipment, the station is a unique monument to the history of the architecture industry in the Ottoman Empire. It pumped to Balmumcu and Beşiktaş – in the direction of Tophane, moving water coming from 20 different pipes in Kağıthane using steam pump machines.

ad6aaf4a-2118-5025-a77a-00c66b5583c0.name: Jildrim postcard
ad6aaf4a-2118-5025-a77a-00c66b5583c0.description: This photographic postcard records a group of travellers gathered in and beside an open railway wagon during the First World War. During the war, the Hijaz Railway and its connected lines became military supply routes. They moved soldiers, labourers, food, weapons, timber, animals and construction material toward Palestine and Sinai. Wartime expansion increased the pressure on locomotives and rolling stock already limited in number. The vehicle was built for goods, yet contemporary railway reports show that freight wagons were also used to move large groups of people when passenger coaches were insufficient, especially during military mobilisation.

af2dcc82-957a-54c2-9a0f-e5e5ba86b4d3.name: Ottoman Clothing Album
af2dcc82-957a-54c2-9a0f-e5e5ba86b4d3.short_description: With the political developments of the 19th century, interest in the East increased steadily in the western world. Everything belonging to the East was the centre of interest for western observers. As a result, close to 160 artists visited Istanbul in the 19th century. Pascal Sébah (1823-86) was a pioneer photographer who worked in Istanbul. Sébah opened a photography studio known as "El Chark " in Pera in 1857. The studio's most successful period started with the Vienna Universal Exhibition in 1873. Sébah formed a partnership with Joaillier Polycarpe in 1885. In 1899, the two partners bought Abdullah Frères's archives. For the Vienna Universal Exhibition in 1873, Pascal Sébah prepared *The Ottoman Clothing Album* to be exhibited at the Ottoman Stand.
af2dcc82-957a-54c2-9a0f-e5e5ba86b4d3.holder: Istanbul University, Nadir Eserler Kütüphanesi (Rare Books Library)

af6de1c1-aac3-5b48-9d6c-1e99228574c4.name: Military personnel records
af6de1c1-aac3-5b48-9d6c-1e99228574c4.description:
The information sheets are part of the medical examination prior to the training of the new recruits. The newly enrolled were destined for the Protectorate which, due to the pressure of public opinion, refused the presence of Spaniards in that area.  
The records, along with a pair of photographs, gathered information on individuals’ social and professional backgrounds, as well as descriptive data and anthropometric values. Those values were used by the Medical Corps to determine the minimum size permitted to enter in the Army, but they were also important according to the existing racial theories in Spain.  
The sheets refer to these soldiers as “Moors” in a generic way, a colloquial and sometimes pejorative term of Latin etymology, which alludes to the population of the Maghreb with no regard to their origin, ethnicity or beliefs.
keywords: Photography; War
