f5b47725-414d-52d8-902a-bee467f7d304.name: *Works for the opening of the Corinth Canal*
f5b47725-414d-52d8-902a-bee467f7d304.short_description:
The Corinth Canal being dug, circa 1885. Photographer unknown.  
The Corinth Canal separates the Peloponnesian peninsula from the Greek. The idea of the canal was revived after Greece gained independence but soon abandoned due to economical reasons. The opening of the Suez Canal in 1869 gave an new impetus and the following year, the Zaimis government passed a law authorising the construction of the canal, which was formally inaugurated on 23 April 1882. Zaimis assigned the project to the Hungarian István Türr who set up the Société Internationale du Canal Maritime de Corinthe but the company failed and the project was finished by the company of Andeas Syngros. The canal was designed by the Hungarian engineer Béla Gerster with the assistance of the French Vincent Dauzants, a chief engineer of the Suez canal.
f5b47725-414d-52d8-902a-bee467f7d304.author: Maria Dimitriadou
keywords: photo; Corinth

f6862c3c-981a-51c4-bde4-011a1cf8bca0.description: The photographer in this picture is Jean-Gabriel Eynard-Lullin, a pioneer of daguerreotypes and stereo-daguerreotypes in Switzerland, who was a prominent figure in international photographic history. As a banker, financial adviser and diplomat, he exerted great influence on politics and culture.

f6a973df-a6b0-51b8-8bb0-fd4026b06319.name: Photograph of Ion Ghica (sitting)
f6a973df-a6b0-51b8-8bb0-fd4026b06319.short_description: In 1848, Ion Ghica was the envoy of the Wallachian revolutionaries to Istanbul, where he remained after the suppression of the revolution. He created connections among the Ottoman officials, being appreciated by Reshid-Pasha (Grand Vizier from 1854), and became a supporter of the Romanian Principalities’ union under Ottoman sovereignty. A former journalist, he devised the project (not realized) for an economic and literary periodical, published in all the languages spoken in the Empire. In 1854 he was appointed governor of the island of Samos, where he took measures against piracy and founded several schools (a middle school, an agricultural school, a marine school and a girls’ institute). His activity earned him the title of “prince”(bey) of Samos, which he received from sultan Abdülmecid in February 1856.

f8ef1a5d-bd50-58f0-8924-3cf66022bfda.name: Inauguration of the Grande Dixence dam
f8ef1a5d-bd50-58f0-8924-3cf66022bfda.description: The water level is shown here rising behind the Grande Dixence dam near Sion (Valais), 18/07/1957; image from the feature produced by the Presse Diffusion Lausanne (PDL) photo agency. Constructed between 1950 and 1964, and commissioned between 1961 and 1965, the dam is located in the Valais commune of Hérémence. The crest of the dam lies at an altitude of 2,365 metres above sea level; this makes the dam Switzerland’s highest-lying construction. The dam wall is 285 metres high, making it the world’s tallest gravity dam. A symbol of Swiss engineering excellence, the Grande Dixence dam is the biggest producer of sustainable energy in Switzerland today. The 1950s and 1960s represented a period of economic and social advancement in Switzerland, and press photographers recorded the changes in full and in detail. Those working for the PDL and Actualités Suisses Lausanne (ASL) agencies focused particularly on the construction boom in the energy and transport sectors, and often also on the societal and political debates, conflicts, and repercussions associated with it. The Swiss National Museum acquired the PDL and ASL archives in 2007. Combined they number around six million images in the form of negatives, prints, and slides. Covering the years from 1937 to 1999, they record the most significant developments during the era of analogue press photography.
f8ef1a5d-bd50-58f0-8924-3cf66022bfda.method_for_datation: Documents. The year and place of production were written on the paper-envelopes that contained the negatives in the archives
f8ef1a5d-bd50-58f0-8924-3cf66022bfda.provenance: Switzerland, Grande Dixence dam in Hérémence near Sion (Valais)
f8ef1a5d-bd50-58f0-8924-3cf66022bfda.obtention: The ASL and PDL archives were bought in 2007
keywords: Photography; Press Photography; Actualités Suisse Lausanne; Presse Diffusion Lausanne; Dam; Grande Dixence; Hérémence; Sion; Vallais

fbde1ba4-0cc0-547e-9260-e7d47c092d47.name: Picture postcard, *Greetings from Pirot*
fbde1ba4-0cc0-547e-9260-e7d47c092d47.description: A picture postcard with the Cyrillic inscription *Pozdrav iz Pirota* (*Greetings from Pirot*) shows a woman from Pirot weaving a kilim, with a child standing by her side. Pirot, a town in south-eastern Serbia, was an important centre of kilim weaving in the Balkans. Pirot kilims were woven on vertical looms (as the one shown in the picture) with a slit weave technique (*klečanje*), which renders both front and back of a weave even and identical. It took one to ten weavers to weave a kilim, depending on its dimensions. The kilims were made of fine, thinly and evenly spun wool which, until 1880’s, was exclusively processed at homes. One of their major characteristics are the studied coloristic effects, achieved by choice and distribution of colours. Natural herb dyes were replaced by the aniline ones at the beginning of the 20th century.
fbde1ba4-0cc0-547e-9260-e7d47c092d47.method_for_datation: Ref. Perać, J., *Razglednice u Srbiji 1895–1914 = Postcards in Serbia 1895–1914*, Belgrade: Museum of Applied Art, 2009.

fc3b1ec9-a4c8-5bb0-8563-67addfda87dd.name: Portrait of the Marquess of Cerralbo in a Turkish Garment
fc3b1ec9-a4c8-5bb0-8563-67addfda87dd.description: The Marquis of Cerralbo and his family visited Istanbul in 1889, and nowadays the Cerralbo Museum holds an interesting variety of pieces bought and collected as souvenirs from the family trip. When visiting a foreign country or city, being portraited by a famous photographer of studio was indispensable. In this case the photographers are the world-renowned Armenian Abdullah Frères, Photographes de S. M. I. le Sultan. This vignetted bust shot albumen portrait of Inocencia Serrano y Cerver, marquise of Cerralbo, shows the playful and aesthetic use of typical Turkish costume in the Abdullah Frères studio, perfect to satisfy the European desire of exoticism.
fc3b1ec9-a4c8-5bb0-8563-67addfda87dd.author: Cecilia Casas Desantes
keywords: Portrait; women; souvenir; memorabilia; orientalism

fc5492b4-b79e-5ab6-acf3-8e4d44f66cbc.name: The villa of Paul Draneht in Oggebbio (Verbania, Italy)
fc5492b4-b79e-5ab6-acf3-8e4d44f66cbc.short_description:
In 1872, Paul Draneht Bey bought a Villa on the Lago Maggiore (Italy), which he remodelled, mixing oriental and European architectural styles. From this postcard, one can see a tower with an Arabic flavour.  
In the interior, there was an “Egyptian hall”, modelled according to the style of an ancient Upper-Egypt temple. The furniture was made by one of the shops in Paris that was making the scenes for the opera *Aida*.
fc5492b4-b79e-5ab6-acf3-8e4d44f66cbc.author: Massimiliano Cremona, Ignazio Galella

fe6fa089-3083-5936-9e90-9d863dea6475.name: Osman Hamdi Bey (During the excavation of Mount Nemrut)
fe6fa089-3083-5936-9e90-9d863dea6475.short_description: In the 19th century, efforts were in place to modernize the Ottoman Empire, as many of the leading statesmen were exposed to Western ideas through education and travel. The museum was founded by decree in 1891 as the Imperial Museum. The first curator and founder of the museum was Osman Hamdi. Hamdi began construction of the main building in 1881, and it achieved its present neo-Greek form in 1908. The architect was Alexander Vallaury. It is one of the prominent structures built in the neoclassical style in Istanbul. Osman Hamdi, during his tenure as museum director, launched the first Turkish scientific excavations. He carried out archaeological excavations at Mount Nemrut, Laguna and Sidon.
keywords: Painting; Osman Hamdi Bey; orientalist Turkish painters,; archaeological excavations

fe87deef-c455-5755-9f18-175550fef06e.name: Opening of the bridge over the Kishon (Qishon) River in the Jezreel Valley (?). A train festooned with Ottoman flags and carrying many pasengers is on the bridge, and dignitaries stand on the track.
fe87deef-c455-5755-9f18-175550fef06e.description: The photograph records an opening ceremony at a railway bridge, tentatively identified as a crossing of the Kishon River, also known as Nahr al-Muqatta‘, in the Jezreel Valley. A train decorated with Ottoman flags and carrying numerous passengers stands on the bridge, while dignitaries gather on the track. Conder and Kitchener described the Kishon as Palestine’s most important river after the Jordan, tracing a course of approximately 23 miles (37 km) from its spring-head west of Mount Tabor to the sea. Their survey records a width of approximately ten yards (9 m) and a depth of four feet (1.2 m) east of Tell el-Kassis in June 1875. Marshy ground and steep banks made crossings difficult along parts of its course, providing geographical context for the construction of railway bridges.
fe87deef-c455-5755-9f18-175550fef06e.bibliography: -Conder. C.R., Kitchener. R.E., ed. Palmer. E. H., Besant. W., The Survey of the Western Palestine Memories Of The Topography, Orography, Hydrography, and Archaeology. Vol. (L), Sheets (VI) for The Committee Of The Palestine Exploration Fund, London (1881)

ffecc84b-856d-5f87-97de-682a1d90e53d.name: *View of Istanbul: the Valide Sultan Mosque and the port*
ffecc84b-856d-5f87-97de-682a1d90e53d.short_description: Pascal Sébah (1823–1886) was a French photographer working in the Ottoman capital Constantinople, where he developed a successful trade selling photographs to European tourists and lovers of Orientalism. The great changes Constantinople underwent towards the end of the 19th century are evident in this image. The Valide Sutlan Mosque dominates the Eminönü port, which had become very prosperous during the Ottoman era thanks to active trading with the West. The construction of the Galata bridge, the Orient Express railway line, and the arrival of steam-boats also contributed to its development.
keywords: Transports; boat; port
